# Code review — SDK-derived coverage subsystem (`feat/sdk-derived-coverage`)

## 1. Verdict

The subsystem works and its plumbing is largely sound: the three extractors produce a stable universe from pinned SDK sources, the pairing walker resolves nearly 2,700 scanner anchors across three providers with 25 tolerated diagnostics and zero fatal ones, and the ratchet, the generated report and the CI wiring all exist and run. Of 134 reported findings, 119 survived verification; none of them shows the pipeline producing garbage, and only a handful move a published percentage by more than a point. The single biggest source of inaccuracy is not a coding defect at all but the **per-provider class rules that decide what is allowed to count as a resource** — they are unevidenced in one direction and asymmetric across providers. On AWS, 991 of 1,614 uncovered rows (61% of the entire gap list) are admitted by a single uncorroborated rule: any depth>0 listing whose element carries an id-like member is a resource, a rule whose own coverage rate is 13.7% against 70.4% for everything else. On Azure, the mirror-image rule is too strict: 517 of 572 `catalog` rows carry the full ARM proxy-resource envelope and are dropped from the denominator entirely, overstating the published Azure headline by roughly 3.6 points, and 13 of them are types disco demonstrably stores. The second-order consequence is that the headline number is not falsifiable from the report itself: the admitting rule is recorded per row in the JSON signals but omitted from `docs/coverage.md`, so a reader cannot see which rule put a row in the denominator. Everything else — refs recall, verify's reason column, the cross-check drift buckets, the scaffold — is smaller, more local, and in several places genuinely broken but cheap to fix.

---

## 2. Bugs

### Critical

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:609` — List ops returning a primitive list with a non-id member name are never candidates

`analyzeOp` counts a list-of-primitives output member as a collection only when the member name matches `idLikeRe`. `sqs:ListQueues` returns `QueueUrls []string` and the Service Reference marks it `IsList=false`, so `listMembers` is 0, the op falls into `Universe.Other`, and the resource never becomes a candidate at all. The failure is total rather than partial: `aws:sqs:queue` — a type disco scans through `NewListQueuesPaginator` — appears in neither the numerator nor the denominator, surviving only as the attribute row `sqs/queue/queueattribute`. Eight List ops fall into this hole, two of them anchored by live disco scanners (`cassandra:ListTypes` is the other). Fix by treating every list-typed output member of a List-verb op as a collection (at minimum when the member stem shares the op noun's `Ident`) and setting `hasIDs` when the element is primitive, or by letting an `sr.resCanon` hit force `isList` for a List verb with any list output; add a `List<Noun>s → <Noun>Urls []string` fixture.

### Major

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:1051` — Pairing `Op`/`Label` is nondeterministic (#57)

`reachableAnchors` does `out[k] = v` while `walkCallees` ranges over the `callees` map, so when two callees anchor the same candidate with different ops, last-write-wins is map-iteration order. Eight runs of `pairing.Walk` in one process produced two distinct content hashes for AWS. The single unstable entry is `scanGuardDutyDetectors`, whose two callees anchor `guardduty/detector` with `GetDetector` and `ListDetectors` respectively. It reaches the user through `buildLabelIndex` (`cmd/coverage_verify.go:363`), which keys `byType` on the pairing label: a verify row's reason for up to four GuardDuty types flips run-to-run between `warning: guardduty:ListDetectors: …` and `no rows`, and because the key set and types are stable, the CI diff of `docs/coverage.md` cannot catch it. Sort callee keys in `walkCallees` and pick a deterministic winner (prefer `IsList`, then the smallest label), and add a regression test asserting `Walk` is byte-stable across two calls.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/refs.go:18` — `handleRe` spills across function bodies, costing 106 listers their refs (#27)

The regex `(?s)func \(client \*\w*Client\) (\w+)HandleResponse\(.*?&result\.(\w+)\)` is lazy, dot-matches-newline and unbounded, so a `HandleResponse` body with no `&result.` (a HEAD `GetEntityTag`) swallows the following function's header and steals its result type; because `FindAllStringSubmatch` is non-overlapping, the real lister then gets no entry. Measured against the live cache, 106 GET collection builders (99 of them paged) lose their result type — 66 in `armapimanagement` alone — after which `extract.go:90` skips them and `refsOf` never runs. Nothing is misclassified and no coverage number moves: the entire loss is the `Refs` column, which degrades the Azure resolver-gap report and the scaffold. Bound each `HandleResponse` body at the next top-level `func` and add a fixture with a HEAD op preceding a List op.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:182` (reported as :251) — Cloud-root membership reads only segment 0, dropping four real cloud APIs (#41)

`rootOf` inspects only the first segment after the version prefix, so APIs whose listers use a generic `{+parent}` expansion (`v1/{v1Id}/{v1Id1}/assets`), carry a non-version static (`v1/admin/projects/…`) or root at `services/{service}` are filtered out of the universe wholesale. Four genuine Google Cloud APIs and roughly 13 listers are absent entirely — Cloud Asset feeds/savedQueries/assets, Service Usage services, all of Pub/Sub Lite, and Service Networking connections/peeredDnsDomains — so a whole product is invisible to a denominator of 1,009 listable GCP collections. It also produces a false `sdk-skew` pairing diagnostic against `quota_scanners.go:140`, claiming `serviceusage.services.list` is not in `serviceusage` at the pinned ref when it plainly is. The reporter's framing that 162 excluded APIs are wrongly dropped does not hold — the other 159 (YouTube, AdSense, DFA reporting, the Cloud Channel reseller API) are correctly excluded. Treat a param-first template as a generic cloud container when the `{+parent}`/`{+name}` parameter names projects/folders/organizations (as `scopeOf` at :289 already does), strip a leading static immediately followed by a cloud root, and add `v1/admin/projects` and `v1/{v1Id}/{v1Id1}` fixtures.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:435` — `TypeRefs` attributes refs by `Row.DiscoType` only, starving and contaminating orphan types (#75)

`TypeRefs` unions a row's refs under `Row.DiscoType`, which on a multi-type pairing can be the arbitrary `bestType` fallback, and it ignores `Row.DiscoTypes` entirely. Fourteen orphan types are starved of refs the same listing plainly provides — all five `aws:docdb:*` and all five `aws:neptune:*` orphans get nothing while `rds/dbinstance`'s 44 refs go to `aws:rds:db-instance`; `aws:amplify:domain` gets nothing while `amplify/domainassociation`'s certificate and branch refs credit `aws:amplify:app` — and `cmd/coverage.go:756` then hides every one of them from `resolvers --missing --with-refs`. In the other direction, eight AWS orphan types are shown with refs picked from an unrelated candidate (`aws:route53:cidr-collection` displays `ResourceId`, which comes from `route53/tag`'s 10-type pairing). The reporter's wider counts (43 AWS types receiving foreign refs, 30 hidden) over-count benign name divergence; 14 + 8 of 1,252 orphan rows is the defensible figure. The fix must stay narrow — give the refs to every `DiscoTypes` entry whose type leaf equals the candidate leaf, and never to a type matching neither the candidate ident nor its leaf — because the doc comment at `inventory.go:416-420` is deliberately guarding the dispatcher case (an Azure firewall FQDN-tag type must not inherit the load balancer's 29 refs).

#### `cmd/coverage.go:301` — `--check-strict` is vacuous when pairing is off (#84)

With `--source-root=` every emitted type with no candidate takes the `in.Pairings == nil` branch at `inventory.go:184-185` and is stamped `pairing-unavailable`, so the `ReasonUnexplained` branch is unreachable and `Summary.Unexplained` is 0 by construction; the gate tests only `Unexplained > 0` and exits 0. Measured: 400 AWS, 12 Azure and 48 GCP emitted types explained by nothing, exit code 0, with `README.md:188-189` promising the opposite. The run does print a stderr warning and the table headline carries `pairing unavailable: name matching only`, so this is a silent pass only for a scripted exit-code consumer — which is exactly what CI is. One guard in `runCoverageServices` (refuse `--check-strict`/`--baseline`/`--write-baseline` when any matrix has `!m.Pairing`, exit 2) closes this and #83 together.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:317` — A baseline written without pairing is a silent low-water mark the ratchet accepts forever (#83)

`--write-baseline` records the name-matching-only covered set when pairing is off and the file carries no pairing marker, so a later pairing-on `--baseline` run reports zero drift: a key that was uncovered in the baseline and is covered now is in `known` and produces no drift, and the percent check only fires on a drop. Reproduced in both directions — a pairing-off baseline fed back with pairing on exits 0 with no stderr at all, while the committed baseline against a pairing-off run exits 1 with 231 `regressed` lines, proving the asymmetry. 278 covered keys lose ratchet protection (AWS 231 including `ec2/address` and `monitoring/alarm`, Azure 3, GCP 44). The realistic entry path is not the exotic CRLF `go.mod` but simply running the binary from a subdirectory of the checkout or from an install, since `defaultSourceRoot` reads `./go.mod` from the cwd only. Add a `pairing` bool to `ProviderBaseline` and compare it; a pairing-off baseline compared against a pairing-off run is self-consistent, so it is mode-mixing that must be refused.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:317` — A partial `--write-baseline` truncates the ratchet and a missing provider is non-fatal (#82)

`NewBaseline` records only the matrices that ran and never merges with an existing file, so `--providers aws --write-baseline docs/coverage-baseline.json` leaves a file whose `jq keys` is exactly `["aws"]`. Feeding that file back across all three providers exits 0, printing only `azure: no-baseline` / `gcp: no-baseline`, because `CompareBaseline` iterates only the fresh matrices and `DriftNoBaseline` is excluded from `Drift.Fatal`. `make gen-coverage TAGS="slim aws"` takes exactly this path. Worse than reported: `make check-coverage` does not backstop it either, because the `Pins:` line-count mismatch between a 1-provider and a 3-provider report routes the Makefile into the warn-only "SDK pins moved" branch instead of the exit-1 stale-doc branch. After one such run, Azure (1,036 listable) and GCP are unchecked and CI stays green. Make `DriftNoBaseline` fatal (or iterate the union of baseline ∪ fresh providers), merge partial writes into the existing file, compare `Pins` line counts before choosing the Makefile branch, and add tests for a partial write and a partial compare.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:269` — The Service Reference date pin is a fetch-time artifact, not a pin (#86)

`serviceReferenceVersion` derives the pin from the newest per-service `modified` stamp in the live index, which changed on 12 of the last 13 days, while `Cache.Ensure` never refetches an existing snapshot and the snapshot directory is keyed on the SDK ref alone. CI keys `actions/cache` on `hashFiles(pins.go, go.mod)`, so any `go.mod`-touching push refetches the catalog under that day's date and the run's pins no longer match the baseline's. Simulated both sides: under identical pins a vanished covered key gives `! regressed` plus `! percent-drop` and exit 1; with a one-day-older service-reference pin the same baseline gives `pins-changed` + `gone-since-baseline` and exit 0. What softens is specific — a covered key vanishing from the candidate set, the percent-drop check, and the `docs/coverage.md` staleness diff for all three providers at once — while a baseline covered key that is merely uncovered now stays fatal. The `regen-coverage` job then commits the regenerated baseline unreviewed. Record the index sha256 (or the derived date) in `pins.go` so the fetch is a real pin, and key the CI cache on the baseline's pins as the cheap mitigation.

#### `internal/sdkinv/cache.go:86` — A snapshot fetched under an older `Keep` filter is treated as complete forever (#112)

`Cache.Ensure` returns the existing directory whenever `Status` finds a readable manifest, and `Status` compares nothing in that manifest against the live `FetchSpec`, so a change to `Keep`/`Dest`/`Source` at an unchanged pin is invisible. This already happened on this branch: `733ed624` kept only `*_client.go`/`models.go`/`response_types.go`, and `ca694f4e` widened it to every non-test `.go` at the same `AzureSDKRef`. Rebuilding the old file set from the live cache and running the shipped binary against it reproduces Azure 378/1558/1759 at 19.52% against the live 386/1573/1785 at 19.70% — 49 keys missing and five spurious disco-only rows, with no fetch and no warning. In CI it is not fully silent but it misdirects: `make check-coverage` hits the "docs/coverage.md is stale" branch and `make gen-coverage` on a correct cache cannot clear it, so CI stays red until someone bumps a pin or evicts the runner cache by hand. Record a spec fingerprint in the manifest, have `Status` return `ErrNotFetched` on mismatch, assert `m.Provider`/`m.Ref`, and add `internal/sdkinv/*/*.go` to the CI cache key.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:222` — The `services[ToLower]` filter silently drops 420 registry entries (#117)

`CrossCheck` keeps a registry entry only when `strings.ToLower(r.Service)` is a key in the universe's service map, but the universe keys by sigv4 name while Service Reference entries carry the IAM prefix and CloudFormation entries the product namespace. Replaying the real cross-check (CFN `ListTypes` plus SR, 4,247 entries) emits 587 registry-only rows while silently discarding 420 entries across 132 services, with nothing printing the dropped set. Re-keying those through a sigv4/arnNamespace/endpointPrefix alias map built from the cached Smithy models resolves 194 of them to services the universe knows under another name — Pinpoint→mobiletargeting (19), Cognito→cognito-idp (18), ApiGatewayV2→apigateway (15), CloudWatch→monitoring (12), EMR→elasticmapreduce, MSK→kafka, OpenSearchServerless→aoss. The result is 52 genuinely-absent registry resources suppressed instead of reported (`AWS::CloudWatch::CompositeAlarm`, `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime`, `AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthorityActivation`) and 16 spurious candidate-only rows. Crucially, relaxing the filter alone adds ~142 *false* registry-only rows, so the fix must be the identity join: have the AWS extractor record which registry service it joined and key `RegistryKey` on it, plus a stderr note naming services dropped for having no counterpart.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:757` — `--with-refs` uses refs as a hide gate, contradicting "refs are hints" (#125)

`if withRefs && len(refs[decl.DiscoType]) == 0 { continue }` turns a lossy hint into the definition of a derived leaf, so every recall gap in `refs.go` and every attribution miss in `TypeRefs` deletes a type from the resolver worklist. AWS hides 361 of 821 orphan types, Azure 70 of 342, GCP 46 of 89 — 477 in total. The root cause is not the filter as a UI choice but `TypeRefs` at `inventory.go:421-424` ignoring `Row.DiscoTypes` (see #75): 81 AWS emitted types are attributed only through that secondary list and get zero refs, and 30 of those are orphans hidden on that basis, including all the DocumentDB and Neptune types whose Smithy elements carry `DBClusterIdentifier`, `KmsKeyId` and `VpcSecurityGroups`. The file even contradicts itself — `cmd/coverage.go:741` says refs are a hint while :757 uses their absence as a hard filter. Fix `TypeRefs` first; then, at minimum, print the hidden count to stderr rather than dropping types invisibly. Do not reword `internal/providers/CLAUDE.md:117` or the README to bless the current behaviour: "a type with no refs is the derived leaf" is false for at least these 30 types.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:261` — An Azure per-subscription failure is recorded as a whole-provider failure (#101)

`azure_scanner.go:314` (and `reportPanic` at :307) report a per-subscription failure as `store.ScanError{Service: "scan", Scope: sub.scopeLabel()}`, `scanrun.go:225` persists it as service `azure:scan`, and `store.ScanErrorEntry` has no `Scope` field so the scope is dropped on the way to the database. In `reason()`, `stripProvider("azure:scan","azure") == wholeScanService`, so the branch fires for every declared type and returns immediately, short-circuiting the warnings loop. Reproduced by inserting one such entry: 417 of 417 Azure types read `scan-error: Error`, including the four `azure:microsoft.entra:*` types, `management-groups` and `subscriptions` — all tenant-scoped and provably independent of any one subscription. The reason column is the entire point of the command, and here it is wrong for every row. Fix both call sites with a distinct label, and add `Scope` to `ScanErrorEntry` (a JSON-column shape change, no migration needed) so verify can tell a subscription failure from a run failure.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:350` — Outside a source checkout, no Azure op-label warning can ever explain a type (#103)

The no-pairing fallback joins a warning by `prefix, _, _ := strings.Cut(label, ":")` against the type's service names. Azure warning labels are all `arm<module>:<Client>.<Method>` — 325 distinct such literals in `internal/providers/azure` — while Azure service names are `microsoft.<ns>`, so the prefix can never match. AWS (`kms:ListKeys`) and GCP (`bigtableadmin:instances.list`) prefixes *are* the service, which is why the same one-line join works for them. Reproduced with a synthetic `azure:armnetwork:VirtualWans.List` warning: from the repo root 48 types are explained; from `/tmp` — the shipped-binary default — zero are, and all 417 read `no rows`. For every end user of the shipped binary, every Azure permission and skip warning degrades to "the tenant has none". Carry the registered service name on the Azure warning (`skipIfAccessDenied` already has subscription context and `serviceEntry.name` is available at the dispatch site) rather than string-munging `"microsoft."+TrimPrefix(prefix,"arm")`, which is wrong for `armappservice`/`armweb`, `armcosmos`/`microsoft.documentdb` and `armresources`.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:347` — With the pairing present, service-named warnings explain nothing (#102)

When the pairing loaded, `explains()` returns `ix.byType[typ][label]` only, with no service fallback. The doc comment's premise — that a label the pairing does not know is a store-level warning — is false: several scanners warn with a *service* name, not an op label (`entra_scanners.go:889` uses `azure:microsoft.entra`, `tenant_scanners.go:406` `azure:tenant-scope`, `management_scanners.go:348` `azure:microsoft.resources`, GCP `cloudidentity`). Measured with synthetic scans in both modes: an Entra permission warning explains 0 types with pairing and 4 without; `gcp:cloudidentity` explains 0 versus 12; `microsoft.resources` 0 versus 3; and `azure:tenant-scope` explains nothing in either mode, so a Lighthouse/WIF tenant-scope skip is never surfaced. The fix must not be a blanket prefix fallback: `cmd/coverage_verify_test.go:215-236` deliberately pins that an unknown label whose prefix is a service (`organizations:root`, a store-level native-id-collision warning) must *not* explain by prefix. Distinguish a service-scoped warning from a store-level one at the source — a kind/scope field on `store.ScanWarning`, or accepting the prefix only when the label has no op-shaped suffix — and handle `azure:tenant-scope`, which is not a service name at all.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:260` — An interrupted scan explains nothing (#104)

`scanrun.go:210-218` appends `ScanErrorEntry{Service: "scan:interrupted", Code: "Canceled"}` with no provider prefix, unlike the per-service loop three lines below. In `reason()`, `stripProvider` leaves it unchanged, it is neither `wholeScanService` nor a service name, and the stored-nothing fallback requires a `provider:` prefix — so all three tests miss. Reproduced: an interrupted AWS scan with no stored rows reports `no rows` for all 1,843 declared types, and since `LatestCompleteScan` accepts `partial`, that scan is the default `--scan-id latest` target immediately after Ctrl-C. The one structured entry that exists precisely to make the interruption queryable is the one entry verify cannot read. Treat `e.Service == "scan:interrupted"` as whole-scan for every provider; note the entry carries no provider, so a multi-provider scan must apply it to all of them.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:201` — `coverage verify --scan-id` rejects the 8-character ids the CLI prints (#97)

`resolveScan` calls `db.GetScan(id)` directly instead of the shared `resolveScanID`, which handles 8–31-character hex prefixes and is used by `diff`, `resources`, `summary`, `tag-coverage` and `scans show`. Reproduced against the sample DB: `disco scans` prints `15115114`, and `coverage verify --scan-id 15115114` fails with `sql: no rows in result set` and exit 1 — for all three ids in that DB. Full 32-hex ids work, so the command is usable only with the form the CLI never shows. `cmd/CLAUDE.md:258` states the rule explicitly ("Any new scan-id-taking command must do the same"). Route the non-`latest` branch through `isScanIDPrefix`/`resolveScanIDPrefix` with the `scan %q not found` wording, and keep the deliberate divergence for `latest`, which must stay `LatestCompleteScan`.

#### `cmd/disco-scaffold/gen.go:89` — The scaffold emits a `registerService` for an already-registered name (#90)

`genScaffold` unconditionally emits `registerService(serviceEntry{name: "<prov>:<svc>", fn: scan<Svc>})` whenever the provider has a known signature, even though `main.go:94-97` has just printed every already-covered candidate for that service — the tool knows the service is scanned. All three providers panic on a duplicate registration at init. Counting only targets where the existing-file guard does not block `--write`, 34 AWS, 123 Azure and 5 GCP services produce a file that kills the provider package's tests and the binary until the line is deleted; in stdout mode it is 321 of the 639 services with uncovered rows. The reporter's worked example (`aws:s3`) is wrong — that one is blocked by the file guard; the live panic path is a registered service with no same-named `<svc>_scanners.go`, such as `azure:microsoft.batch`, `gcp:spanner`, `aws:events` or `aws:elasticloadbalancing`. A second mechanism compounds it: the emitted `func scan<Svc>` collides with an existing function for services whose scanner lives under another file name (`gcp:spanner` → `scanSpanner` already at `databases_scanners.go:909`), which is a compile error rather than a panic. Consult the registry before emitting either the registration or the stub.

#### `cmd/disco-scaffold/gen.go:56` — The scaffolded type string drops the candidate's parent path (#91)

`resourceSegment` takes only the text after the last `/`, so both the type string and the const name lose the parent, and two candidates sharing a leaf produce identical declarations. `disco-scaffold azure:microsoft.compute` emits `TypeMicrosoftComputeRuncommand` and `TypeMicrosoftComputeDiagnosticruncommand` twice each, from `virtualmachines/runcommands` and `virtualmachinescalesets/virtualmachines/runcommands`; `format.Source` does not catch it (duplicate consts parse fine), so the tool reports success and the file fails to compile — refuting `gen.go:44`'s claim that the output "compiles as-is". 41 Azure and 17 GCP services are in this state; AWS keys are flat enough to escape. Separately, 2,568 of 3,961 uncovered rows are depth>0 children whose emitted type drops the parent, against a repo convention that is explicitly colon-path for Azure children. The reporter's cited test failure is wrong — `TestNoDoubleDeclaredTypes` only flags a `registerType`/legacy-`emits` clash, so a pasted duplicate `registerType` is accepted silently and diverges the redaction rules instead of failing. Include parent segments in both the const name and the type string, and verify emitted strings against `prov.Emits()` before writing.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:355` — Verb-only operations produce malformed keys (#5)

`splitVerb` returns an empty noun for operations like `Search`, and `indexModel` still builds `<svc>/` keys from them. Two such keys are classified `resource` and counted in the denominator, and `docs/coverage.md` ships `resource-explorer-2/` and `sagemaker/` as uncovered resources plus `datazone/domain/` as an attribute row; the derived `RegistryKey` becomes `sagemaker::`. `conformance.checkCandidate` only tests the `<service>/` prefix, so empty-leaf keys, `*/features` and keys containing `{`, `?` or `$` all pass the contract. Route empty-noun ops to `Other` (or take the noun from the SR action's single target resource), and reject keys with an empty last segment, `//`, braces, `?`, `=`, `$` or a service outside `[a-z0-9.-]+`, running the check on live universes rather than only fixtures.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:414` — Duplicate operation shapes plus unstable `SortOps` make the universe non-deterministic (#6)

The op name is taken as the shape id after `#`, so `healthlake.json`'s two namespaces yield two `Operations` with identical `Label` and `Module` but different `Required`, and `sdkinv.SortOps` uses an unstable `sort.Slice` keyed on Label+Module, so their order flips between runs. Three consecutive `Extract` runs produced two different universe JSONs (`ResourceArn` ↔ `ResourceARN` swapping in `Required`), and eight runs split 5/3 between the two spellings. Any golden-file comparison or `Required`-derived output is flaky as a result. Iterate shapes in sorted id order and dedupe ops sharing Label+Module in the extractor, and make `SortOps` a total order over (Name, Path, Required, IsList, Paged) or use `sort.SliceStable`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:561` — The fallback parent is the alphabetically last id member (#9)

With several required id members, `lineage` takes the last sorted stem and `pickParent` breaks ties by catalog order; `scopeParams` lists only `AccountId`/`Region`, so `AwsAccountId` and asynchronous `JobId` handles become parents, and `idStem` collisions let the last writer win. 64 resource candidates are mis-parented — `codecatalyst/workflow` is parented to `space` rather than `project`, `datazone/assetfilter` to `domain`, `apigateway/methodresponse` to itself at depth 4 — and 465 rows name a parent that is not a candidate key, including 15 QuickSight rows under `quicksight/awsaccount`, eight Rekognition and five Textract rows under job handles. Resolve parents in a pass after indexing, preferring existing entries then the deepest, never self; keep every resource per `idStem` and pick by op-noun match; match scope params case-insensitively; and treat `job` stems with no catalogued job resource as handles under a `job-handle` signal.

### Minor

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:95` — `qualifierRe` lacks `As`, splitting `servicecatalog/product` (#25)

`splitVerb` trims only `For|By|In|Of|Within|From`, so `SearchProductsAsAdmin` yields the noun `ProductsAsAdmin`, which matches neither the SR resource `Product` nor a write noun. The result is a pair of wrong rows: `servicecatalog/product` reads **uncovered with no disco type**, while `servicecatalog/productsasadmin` sits in `excluded` yet carries the live type `aws:servicecatalog:cloud-formation-product` — and `servicecatalog_scanners.go:236` really does drive `NewSearchProductsAsAdminPaginator`, so the pairing is right and only the noun split is wrong. Enumerating every AWS op whose noun contains `As[A-Z]` at a non-zero offset across all 431 models gives six hits, so adding `As` to the alternation has a very small blast radius, and `ImportAsProvisionedProduct`/`MarkAsArchived` are unaffected because their `As` sits at offset 0.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/refs.go:27` — `loadModels` reads only `models.go` (#33)

The path is hard-coded to `models.go` and errors return nil, so the three modules shipping the older `zz_generated_models.go` layout (`armmachinelearningservices`, `armvideoanalyzer`, `armworkloadmonitor`) lose every ref: 25 rows, nine of them non-excluded. Recoverable value is small — `microsoft.media/videoanalyzers` gains four real refs, the others none. The fix as proposed is necessary but not sufficient and would silently produce garbage on its own: the older layout puts the struct tag on the field line, so `fieldRe`'s trailing capture swallows it and every `*string` test fails. Glob `models.go|zz_generated_models.go` **and** cut the field type at the first backtick. The side note is also right: `keepARMFile`'s `base != "models_serde.go"` check does not match `zz_generated_models_serde.go`, so those files are cached for nothing.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:226` — `scopeOf` sees only the segments before the namespace (#34)

`scopeOf` is called with `segs[:nsIdx]` and tests for an extension resource with `s.Param && i == 0`, so a management-group template whose `managementGroups/{groupId}` pair sits *after* the namespace reports `tenant`, and the generic `.../providers/{parentProviderNamespace}/{parentResourceType}/{parentResourceName}/providers/<ns>/...` extension form is missed because its `{param}` is at index 5. Recomputing over every candidate gives four rows wrong by the first mechanism and 18 by the second, ten of which are uncovered rows published in `docs/coverage.md` with the wrong scope (`microsoft.chaos/targets` at :2532 reads `resource-group`, `microsoft.serialconsole/serialports` at :3492 reads `subscription`). Feed the whole template to `scopeOf` and return `ScopeExtension` for a `providers/{param}` pair anywhere in the prefix; because `ScopeExtension` outranks everything in `scopeRank`, re-baselining `docs/coverage.md` belongs in the same commit.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pathtmpl.go:12` — `ParseTemplate` keeps query strings (#35)

Five `urlPath` literals in the Azure cache carry a `?query`, and since a segment is only a param when it both starts with `{` and ends with `}`, `{apiId}?export=true` parses as a static, the template stops looking like an item path, and the GET is admitted as a collection. Four junk keys result, all in `excluded/non-resource`, two of them item GETs (`APIExport.Get`, `WorkspaceAPIExport.Get`) counted as collection listers. No percentage moves; the cost is polluted excluded listings and per-service op counts. Cut the template at the first `?` inside `ParseTemplate` so these merge into the existing `apis`/`operationresults` entries.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:140` — Namespace search picks the parameterised `providers` (#37)

The loop walks down to the *last* segment equal to `providers` and sets namespace `*` when the next segment is a param, so `/subscriptions/{id}/providers/Microsoft.Features/providers/{resourceProviderNamespace}/features` discards the real namespace. Exactly one row is affected (`*/features`, filed under a fabricated service that does not even appear in the services list), and it is `excluded/catalog` either way. The proposed fix is incomplete on its own: preferring the last `providers` with a static successor yields the key `microsoft.features/providers/features`, so the trailing `providers/{param}` pair must also be handled as a scope pair in `StripScopes`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:68` — A `.go` file directly under `sdk/resourcemanager` panics the extractor (#38)

`module := rel[:strings.LastIndex(rel, "/")]` slices with `-1` when `rel` has no directory, and `keepARMFile` would admit such a file (`sdk/resourcemanager/doc.go` passes every test). Confirmed as a genuine panic with a standalone program (`slice bounds out of range [:-1]`), inside the `WalkDir` callback with no recover, so it aborts the whole command. No root-level `.go` file exists at the pinned commit, so this is latent robustness rather than a live defect: skip a `rel` with no `/`, or require `path.Dir(rel)` to have two components.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:346` (reported as :415) — `parentKey` does not lower-case top-level node names (#42)

The top-level branch returns `dc.Name + "/" + n` with `n` taken verbatim from Discovery (camelCase), while keys are built lower-cased at :202 and the nested branch at :334 does lower-case. Exactly 10 candidates carry a `Parent` that is not a key but whose lower-cased form is — `dns/changes`, `dnskeys`, `managedzoneoperations` and `resourcerecordsets` pointing at `dns/managedZones`, plus five Compute rows. `README.md:89` defines `Parent` as the parent candidate's key and `conformance.go:65` asserts exactly that on fixtures, so this is a contract violation rather than a preference. One-line fix, plus a live assertion that every `Parent` resolves, which would also catch #43.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:334` (reported as :403) — Nested parent names an ancestor that is not a candidate (#43)

`parentKey` returns the doc-path prefix for any nested node whether or not that prefix is itself a candidate, so 114 of 1,850 GCP candidates carry an unresolvable parent pointer (17 catalog, 47 non-resource, 50 resource); 10 of those are #42's case bug, leaving 104 genuinely dangling ancestors — `appengine/apps/services` pointing at a non-existent `appengine/apps`, `firestore/databases/collectiongroups/indexes`, `osconfig/instances/inventories`. The reporter's claim that `Depth` is inflated does not hold: `Depth` comes from `len(rp.Parents)`, the URL template's parent-id count, and is correct for these rows. Resolve `Parent` to the nearest ancestor prefix that is a candidate and clear it when none exists, keeping `Depth` — note `conformance.go:103` currently ties `Depth > 0` to `Parent != ""`, so that check needs relaxing — and add the assertion to `TestExtract_Live`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/refs.go:76` — `element()` picks the alphabetically-first array-of-`$ref` (#46)

The response's property names are sorted and the first array-of-`$ref` wins, which is alphabetical rather than semantic. Running the real code over the pinned cache, `ListJobsResponse {failedLocation, jobs, nextPageToken}` picks `FailedLocation` and yields zero refs, where walking `Job` yields 17 (`projectId`, `replaceJobId`, `createdFromSnapshotId`, `environment.workerPools.subnetwork`, `environment.serviceKmsKeyName`, and more). Eight candidates have more than one array-of-`$ref` property and five pick the wrong element, but only `dataflow/jobs` — a covered type — actually loses data; the others yield zero refs either way or fall back to a legacy sibling schema. Prefer the array property whose `Ident` matches the collection noun or the item schema name, then the richest item schema, then the current alphabetical fallback.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:327` — The version-prefix strip only recognises `^v\d` (#49)

`template()` strips through the first segment matching `^v\d`; Deployment Manager's alpha document has version `alpha` and flat paths like `deploymentmanager/alpha/projects/…`, so nothing is stripped, `rootOf` returns `deploymentmanager`, no lister is cloud-rooted and the whole document is dropped. Sweeping all 654 cached documents, exactly one is excluded solely by this rule, costing seven listers. Nothing in today's report is wrong — every alpha collection also exists in v2 or v2beta, and v2 is stable so no preview-only marking changes — and the reporter's `sdk-skew` scenario is hypothetical since disco does not scan Deployment Manager. One-line fix: strip through the first segment matching `^v\d` **or** equal to `dc.Version`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:183` — Non-cloud versions of an included API are silently dropped (#50)

`indexDoc` returns `false, nil` when no lister is cloud-rooted, discarding both the listers and the collected `others`, while `Extract` only deletes the API from `excluded` — so the comment claiming that an API rooted in a cloud container in one version is in the universe in every version is not what the code does for that version's own data. Nineteen `(api, version)` documents of cloud APIs are dropped this way, totalling 49 listers. No live row is wrong, and the one way this could corrupt the report — a dropped *stable* version leaving its API marked preview-only — does not occur, because the four candidate v1 documents contain only `operations`/`media` nodes. Prefer the documentary half of the fix: reword the comment and emit a diagnostic naming the skipped pairs. Indexing every version would add roughly 16 mostly junk candidates and make the report noisier.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/refs.go:83` — `element()` recurses through `additionalProperties` with no cycle guard (#53)

`element()` recurses into `ss.element(p.AdditionalProperties.Ref)` with neither a `seen` set nor a depth bound, unlike `walk()` three dozen lines below, which carries both — the asymmetry is the tell. True self-cycles exist in the pinned cache today: `discovery/v1 JsonSchema`, `BackendRule` in five `service*` APIs, and `dataflow BoundedTrieNode`. None is currently reachable from a list response in a cloud-rooted document, so a full `Extract` completes; the exposure is the next pin bump, where a stack overflow is a fatal, unrecoverable abort of `disco coverage` and of `make check-coverage`. The reporter's cited examples (aiplatform `Schema.properties`, bigquery `QueryParameterValue.structValues`) are diamonds, not cycles, and already terminate. Thread `walk()`'s `seen` map through `element()`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:59` — `zones`/`regions` are stripped even when the node is a real collection (#55)

`scopeNames` strips every `zones/{zone}` pair, but Dataplex nests assets and entities under `lakes/{lake}/zones/{zone}` while `dataplex/lakes/zones` is itself a create-capable resource candidate. Five live rows carry the wrong key, parent and depth as a result, each understated by one level and parented to the lake instead of the zone, and `dataplex/lakes/actions` additionally merges two distinct API collections into one row, leaving the GCP denominator one candidate short. A probe over the whole universe bounds the collateral precisely: of 71 candidate pairs whose stripped scope node is itself a create-capable candidate, 66 are the intended container cases (organizations, billing accounts, customers) and exactly five are Dataplex. Prefer the narrow fix — strip `zones`/`regions` only in the compute-style `projects/{p}/(zones|regions)/{x}` shape — since the general variant would reshape the 66 legitimate cases the moment a container collection grows a `create` method.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:361` — A caller's anchor can explain a callee's type (#59)

`reachableTypes` unions callee types to depth 3 and `emit` stamps that whole set onto every anchored op, so a type stored by an anchorless callee is reported as `emits` under whatever op the caller happens to call. Reproduced with a fixture in a repo copy: `scanDispatchWithAnchor` calls `ListAliases` then an anchorless `scanHidden(st)` that stores `TypeHidden`, and the pairing reports `emits widgets/alias types=[aws:widgets:hidden]` with the type absent from the unpaired map — while the sibling fixture that is never called is correctly `unexplained`, which is precisely the invariant `adversarial_scanners.go:76` asserts. The live impact is nil: of 2,508 type constants across the three providers, only 24 are stored exclusively by functions with no own anchor, and every one is explained by a legitimate mechanism (typeless-lister promotion, the `derived` path, other-op, skew, non-SDK). The regression scenario is also still caught, by the baseline's fatal covered→uncovered check rather than by `--check-strict`. A narrow fix — route a callee-stored type through orphan/derived when neither it nor anything below it anchors or receives the caller's listing output — must not be combined with dropping the depth cap (#62), which would make over-attribution far worse.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:393` — A `label` pairing marks its types paired, so the two gates give different reasons (#61)

`Unpaired`'s switch special-cases only `other`/`skew` and falls through to `paired[t] = true` for kind `label`, while `pairingKinds` in `inventory.go:105` deliberately excludes `label` and the disco-only branch defaults to `unexplained`. Reproduced with a stale-label fixture: the walker reports the type as paired and the matrix reports it `unexplained`. The claimed gate asymmetry does not hold — `TestScannerOpLabelsResolve` treats `label-no-anchor` as fatal, so the provider test fails too — what disagrees is the *reason* each surface gives, which points CI at the wrong thing. Zero live rows: all three providers currently have zero `label` pairings. Skip `label` in `Unpaired`, or emit label pairings with a nil `Types` slice.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:127` — `calleeDepth=3` turns a correct scanner into a fatal `unexplained` (#62)

Reproduced exactly: a scanner anchoring `ListGizmos` whose store call sits four package-local hops down yields `sidecar … types=[]` plus `UNPAIRED aws:widgets:deep = unexplained`, and both gates then fire on a scanner that is in fact correct, with a message naming neither the depth cut-off nor the storing function. Zero live rows — `unexplained` is 0 for all three providers and every live `sidecar` pairing function is a genuine list-only helper. The proposed fix is wrong as stated: the depth cap is load-bearing against over-attribution, and dropping it would union every transitively reachable type into every anchored op, making #59, #63 and #64 dramatically worse. Continue past the cap only through callees that anchor nothing themselves, or raise the cap behind an explicit constant, and make the message name the deepest anchorless function that stored the type.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:159` — `matched-by-name` overrides contrary pairing evidence (#69)

The default branch consults only `byIdent` — never `in.Unpaired`, never `accounted` — and sets `accounted[t] = true`, which suppresses the type's disco-only row and therefore its contribution to `Summary.Unexplained`, the number `--check-strict` exits on. Since the ratchet keys on `coveredKeys`, a scanner that loses its listing call while keeping its `Type` constant stays covered *and* keeps `Unexplained` at 0, so both gates stay green. That masking hole is real, but the impact is far smaller than reported: there are 39 `matched-by-name` rows (AWS 20, Azure 5, GCP 14, not 31), only five of which name a type the pairing explains otherwise, and in all five the covered verdict is the better answer — disco really does store those resources. The reporter's headline examples are wrong: the nine Compute `region-*` rows are correct recoveries via `Autoscalers.AggregatedList`. And no provider currently has a single `unexplained` type, so the masking class is empty today. The minimal correct fix is to stop the name match suppressing the regression signal — when `in.Pairings != nil` and `in.Unpaired[t] == ReasonUnexplained`, do not name-match — leaving other-op and sdk-skew matches alone; the wholesale fix would flip five currently-correct rows to uncovered.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:112` — `Matrix.Pairing` is derived from a nil slice, not from whether the walk ran (#78)

`pairing.Walk` never initialises `res.Pairings` and `dropEmittedFromDerived` returns nil for a nil input, so a walk that parses fine but anchors nothing is indistinguishable from "no scanner source". Reproduced with a fake source root containing one empty file: exit 0, `"pairing": false`, 400 AWS disco-only rows all reasoned `pairing-unavailable`, `unexplained: 0` — `--check-strict` vacuous. The hole only opens on a *total* pairing collapse, and `make check-coverage` still fails in that state through the baseline percent ratchet (AWS drops 50.3% → 43.2%) and the stale-docs diff, which is why this is minor rather than a second copy of #84. Add an explicit `Inputs.Paired` bool set by `InputsFromCache`, which already knows whether the scanner directory was empty, or have `Walk` return a non-nil empty slice.

#### `internal/coverage/baseline.go:151` — A vanished *uncovered* key is never reported (#81)

`CompareBaseline` walks `pb.CoveredKeys` for keys that are no longer candidates but never walks `pb.UncoveredKeys`, and the percent check only fires on a drop, so a rule edit that reclassifies uncovered candidates out of the denominator produces no drift line of any kind while the mirror case for covered keys produces `DriftRegressed`/`DriftGoneSince`. `baseline_test.go` covers neither. The consequence is narrower than reported: `make check-coverage` does not pass silently under identical pins, because the gaps-filtered `docs/coverage.md` loses those rows and its headline changes, so the stale-docs diff exits 1. The genuine gap is that `CompareBaseline` alone never reports the shrink, and is fully silent once pins have moved (#86), where the doc diff is warn-only. Walk `pb.UncoveredKeys` too, emit a denominator-shrunk drift, and add the missing test.

#### `Makefile:55` — `gen-coverage` truncates `docs/coverage.md` before the run succeeds (#88)

The recipe redirects into the committed file, and because `docs/coverage.md` is not the rule's target, GNU make does not restore it when the `go run` fails — reproduced, leaving a 0-byte file with make exiting 2. Any failure of the generator on a branch (compile error, unreadable SDK cache after `sdk-fetch` succeeded) empties a 3,900-line committed report, recoverable only with `git checkout`. The other two halves of the finding do not stand: `dist/coverage.md.tmp` is gitignored and re-truncated on the next run, and the `--write-baseline` concern is effectively unreachable since the write happens after all fallible extraction and `gen-coverage` passes neither `--baseline` nor `--check-strict`. Write to a temp path and `mv` on success.

#### `.github/workflows/ci.yaml:75` — `regen-coverage` pushes from a stale checkout (#89)

The job checks out `github.sha` with no `ref` or `fetch-depth` and runs a bare `git push` with no fetch or rebase; the concurrency group serialises the jobs but never refreshes the checkout, so a run whose sha is no longer the tip of main gets a non-fast-forward rejection and, under `set -euo pipefail`, a red job. Two preconditions both apply and the finding states neither: two pushes close enough together that the earlier run's regen step lands after the later push, *and* a regeneration that actually changes the files, since the step exits 0 on byte-identical output. The claimed impact is overstated — the later run checks out a superset commit and pushes successfully, so main converges on a correct report; the whole observable effect is a spuriously red job. `git pull --rebase origin main` before pushing. (Medium confidence: the mechanism is plain from the file, the frequency was not reproducible without push rights.)

#### `cmd/disco-scaffold/main.go:108` — `--write` ignores `--source-root` (#92)

The output path is built as `filepath.Join("internal","providers",provName,service+"_scanners.go")` relative to the cwd, while `*sourceRoot` only reaches `inventory()`. Reproduced by running the built tool from a scratch directory with a matching layout and `--source-root` pointing at the real repo: the pairing correctly used the repo (it listed the nine already-covered `run` candidates) and the file landed in the scratch tree, with the tool reporting success — and printing only the relative path, so the wrong-tree write is not obvious from the output. The existing-file guard checks the same wrong path, so it fails to protect the intended target too. Join `*sourceRoot`, or refuse `--write` when it is empty or not the cwd.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:205` — `defaultSourceRoot` silently disables pairing on a CRLF `go.mod` (#94)

The check requires the literal prefix `"module github.com/icearp/disco-cli\n"`. Reproduced: with CRLF line endings the `--source-root` flag shows no default; with LF it shows the directory. The repo has no `.gitattributes`, so a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` — the Git-for-Windows installer default — produces exactly that file, after which AWS reads 43.2% instead of 50.3%, disco-only jumps from 0 to 400 rows, and `make check-coverage` exits 1 with hundreds of `regressed` lines. It is not silent, though: the run prints `no --source-root; pairing unavailable` per provider and the markdown headline says so too, so restate this as "a CRLF `go.mod` defeats the sniff and the ratchet fails loudly with degraded numbers". `TrimSpace` the first line or use `modfile.ModulePath`, and add a `.gitattributes` entry.

#### `cmd/coverage_sdk.go:139` — `sdk status`/`fetch` accept any `--output` and emit no JSON error envelope (#95)

`sdk status -o csv` and `-o bogus` both print the human tabwriter table and exit 0, while every sibling command validates the format up front and returns `unknown --output format %q`. `sdk fetch -o json --providers nope` prints a plaintext error and exits 1 with no envelope, because `maybeStructuredError` is used in `coverage.go` and `coverage_verify.go` but nowhere in this file, so a `-o json | jq` pipeline sees empty stdout. One nuance: `sdk status -o json` does work; it is the validation that is missing there, and both JSON output and the error envelope that are missing on `fetch`. No data is wrong; this is CLI consistency.

#### `cmd/coverage_sdk.go:78` — `--providers` case handling differs across subcommands (#96)

`coverage sdk fetch/status` lower-case and trim the provider name before lookup, while `coverage services`, `coverage verify` and `coverage resolvers` do a raw map lookup against `coverage.Get`. Observed: `sdk status --providers AWS` prints the aws row; `services --providers AWS --services kms` fails with `provider "AWS" has no coverage support`. The same split applies to whitespace padding. Normalise inside the registries (`coverage.Get`/`sdkinv.Get` lower and trim their argument) rather than at each of the four call sites, keeping the existing unknown-name error text.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:267` — The stored-nothing fallback pre-empts a later exact match (#98)

`reason()` tests the exact/whole-scan match and the stored-nothing fallback inside the same loop iteration, so the first provider-prefixed error entry short-circuits the rest of the list. Reproduced against a copied DB with errors `[{aws:iam, AccessDenied}, {aws:scan, Canceled}]` and nothing stored: 1,828 of 1,843 rows read `scan-error: AccessDenied (iam) (us-west-2)` and only the 15 IAM types are correct, while the whole-scan `Canceled` entry never surfaces at all. The precondition — zero rows stored plus at least two error entries in an unlucky order — is plausible on an account where everything failed, though the live scans on disk do not hit it. Two passes: exact service and whole-scan matches first, then the provider-prefix fallback.

#### `internal/sdkinv/fetch.go:215` — `fetchJSONIndex` returns on an unsafe entry while download goroutines are still running (#113)

Entry names are validated inside the goroutine-launching loop and the error path returns before `g.Wait()`. Reproduced with a fake index whose third entry is `../evil` after two entries pointing at a slow handler: `Ensure` returned in 1 ms, the deferred `os.RemoveAll(tmp)` emptied the cache root, and four seconds later the still-running goroutines had recreated the directory through `writeEntry`'s `MkdirAll` and written both files into it. Because `g.Wait()` is never called, the errgroup's context is never cancelled either, so the downloads are not even aborted. The observed failure is therefore a stale `.tmp-<provider>-*` tree that nothing sweeps, not the reported `ENOTEMPTY`. It needs a malformed or hostile upstream index, and the only production caller returns the error straight to cobra, so the process usually exits within milliseconds. Validate every entry before the `g.Go` loop.

#### `internal/sdkinv/cache.go:93` — Fetch uses an HTTP client with no response-header timeout (#114)

`Ensure` defaults to `&http.Client{}` and `httpGet` sets no deadline beyond the context; `cmd/coverage_sdk.go` passes cobra's context, which only a signal cancels, and neither CI job declares `timeout-minutes`, so the GitHub 6-hour default applies. The claim that "nothing bounds a request" is too strong — `http.DefaultTransport` already bounds dial at 30 s and the TLS handshake at 10 s, and the absence of an overall `Client.Timeout` is deliberate and documented at `cache.go:88` for large archives. What is genuinely unbounded is the wait for response headers and any mid-body stall. Set `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (and an idle-read deadline) on a custom transport while keeping no overall timeout, and add `timeout-minutes` to the CI jobs. Worth noting the project already bounds its other network path with `--timeout` at `cmd/coverage.go:156`, which makes this an oversight rather than a stated policy.

#### `internal/providers/aws/aws_coverage.go:73` — `canonResource` strips the `Resource` suffix after `Ident` (#116)

`canonResource` calls `sdkinv.Ident` first — which ends with `TrimRight(c, "es")` — and only then trims `resourc`, so the surviving stem never passes back through the tail-strip: `ThemeResource` → `theme` while the candidate leaf `theme` → `them`, and the two never meet. Replaying over the live SR cache, eight `*Resource` names key differently under trim-before-`Ident` and seven of them then match a real candidate. Confirmed end to end in a live `--cross-check` run: seven spurious registry-only rows (`AWS::amplifyuibuilder::ThemeResource`, three `AWS::drs::*`, three `AWS::mgn::*`) and four spurious candidate-only rows, 11 of 1,993 drift rows. `TestCanonicalKey` pins the suffix case with `Component`/`ComponentResource` — a stem ending in `t`, immune to the tail-strip — which is exactly why this slipped through. Trim on the raw name before `Ident` (guarding an empty stem) and add a case whose stem ends in `e` or `s`.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:211` — `candidate-only` is computed from `Class` alone, so preview-only candidates are reported as drift (#119)

`CrossCheck` selects candidate-only rows on `c.Class == ClassResource`, while `BuildInventory` buckets `preview-only` candidates as `excluded` before the class switch ever runs — `preview-only` is a signal, not a class, so nothing removes them from the drift set. Joining the live GCP drift output against the universe gives an intersection of exactly 20 of 34 candidate-only rows (five `sql/*`, seven `datalabeling`, two `healthcare` annotation stores, two `remotebuildexecution`, and others), so the same report both excludes a candidate as out of scope and re-reports it as drift. This is the opt-in diagnostic only — never `docs/coverage.md`, the baseline or `--check-strict` — hence minor. Take the first half of the fix only: build the candidate-only set from rows bucketed covered/uncovered. The "skip empty-leaf keys" half is unsupported; zero of 1,850 GCP candidates produce such a key.

#### `internal/sdkinv/all/all_test.go:71` — `TestInventoryWalkTime`'s 10-second per-provider bound will flake (#132)

Baseline on a 12-core machine is roughly 2 s per provider (5.9 s for the whole test at `GOMAXPROCS=4`), and extraction is I/O-bound so lowering `GOMAXPROCS` alone barely moves it. Under CPU contention (24 spinners, `GOMAXPROCS=2`) the test failed outright: `azure: extract took 10.892007732s`. The test does run in CI — the workflow restores or fetches the SDK cache under `XDG_CACHE_HOME` before `go test ./...`, which runs packages concurrently on a shared runner — with only 1.7–5x headroom on a hard `t.Errorf`. The scenario does not need a cold cache, just contention. It is not release-blocking (the release workflow's test job runs no `sdk-fetch`, so the test skips), but it is a flaky gate on every PR and push, and `regen-coverage` has `needs: test`. Raise the bound to ~60 s or make it opt-in, keeping the ≥500-candidate assertion that actually guards the extractor.

---

## 3. Accuracy improvements

Grouped by root cause; within each group, the entry that moves the most live rows comes first. Severities are the verifiers'.

### 3.1 The AWS resource-admission rules (the denominator's composition) — structural

This is the largest single source of inaccuracy in the subsystem. Four independent rules decide whether an AWS listing becomes a resource, and the report neither shows which rule fired nor states what the denominator means.

#### `docs/coverage.md:3` — The headline does not say what its denominator admits (major, #127)

`classify` admits **any** depth>0 listing whose element carries id-like members as `ClassResource`, with no Service Reference corroboration, whereas the depth-0 path requires `sr.writeNoun` before admitting. The consequence, counted on the live matrix: 991 of 1,614 uncovered rows (61% of the gap list, 30.5% of the 3,250-row denominator) are admitted by that one rule, whose coverage rate is 13.7% against 70.4% for every other rule. Whole services are unactionable as a result — `resiliencehub` reads 10.3% because 28 of its 35 rows are analysis output and run records (alarm recommendations, compliance drifts, test runs, failure-mode findings), none of which meets the README's own `resource` definition. Four further uncovered rows are outright false gaps for types disco stores under a differently-`Ident`ed name (`lambda/functionversion`, `servicecatalog/product`, `mediaconnect/entitlement`, `profile/calculatedattribute`). Re-running the deleted reconcile report gives 265 skip-labelled keys now counted uncovered, not the reporter's 258. Close the depth asymmetry — require the same SR corroboration at depth>0 that depth 0 already requires — state the denominator's definition in the report header, and split the headline by admitting rule. Do **not** keep a labelled-negatives fixture from the deleted skip list; `CLAUDE.md` forbids hand lists. (Medium confidence: the ≥54.8% figure depends on accepting the retired skip list as ground truth, which the verifier did not arbitrate.)

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:281` — `writable-noun` accepts any non-tagging write verb (major, #10)

`indexSR` records the noun of every `IsWrite` action — `Update`, `Modify`, `Enable`, `Disable`, `Set`, `Export`, `Start` — and `classify` then turns any depth-0 lister with that noun into a resource, contrary to the documented create/delete rule of thumb. 348 uncovered depth-0 rows carry the signal, 134 of them with no create-shaped write at all: `ec2/idformat` (admitted by `ModifyIdFormat`), `ec2/vpcclassiclink`, `eks/clusterversion` (`UpdateClusterVersion`), `rds/certificate` (`ModifyCertificates`), `account/region`, every `compute-optimizer/*recommendation` (admitted by an `Export`), every `backup/*job` (admitted by a `Start`). These are settings and toggles; no scanner can ever close them, so they are permanent denominator ballast. Fill `writeNoun` only from lifecycle verbs and record a separate `mutable` signal for setting verbs so those nouns fall through to catalog or attribute.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:429` — `shape-list` turns a single-subject detail read into a lister (major, #11)

`shapeList := listVerbs[verb] && o.listMembers >= 1` fires for any `Get`/`Describe` of one subject whose output merely contains a nested list, overriding the Service Reference's `IsList=false`. The override is deliberate and load-bearing — 516 covered rows depend on it, and `internal/sdkinv/CLAUDE.md:95` records that trusting the SR alone left 269 scanner types unpaired — so the reporter's framing is wrong in both directions: the named "phantom resources" `kendra/index` and `ecs/taskset` are covered and real, and the proposed gate (require a List verb, a plural noun or `smithy.api#paginated`) would demote them. The indisputable residue is the singular-noun subset: 650 uncovered rows carry `shape-list`, 280 of them with a single `Get`/`Describe` op and 90 of those with a singular noun, of which 26 are unambiguously sub-state (`lambda/functionconfiguration`, `guardduty/organizationconfiguration`, `s3/bucketnotificationconfiguration`, `ec2/capacityreservationusage`, several `*compliancesummary` and `*readinesssummary` rows). Keep the override, but when the noun is singular **and** the op has a required id naming its own subject **and** the SR catalog has no resource of that noun, classify `attribute` with a `detail-read` signal.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:91` — `idLikeRe` is case-sensitive (major, #12)

The regex matches only PascalCase suffixes, so camelCase-modelled services — AppSync, DataZone, Bedrock, EKS, Grafana, Lex, Cognito — whose members are literally `id`, `arn` or `name` never set `hasIDs`, and `classify` demotes their child collections to `attribute` via `id-less-collection`, dropping them out of the denominator entirely. Joining all 523 `id-less-collection` rows against the Smithy element members and counting those with no PascalCase id but a case-insensitive one reproduces the reporter's number exactly: 65 rows across 41 services, of which 48 land in `attribute`, 15 uncovered and 2 covered. Four of the demoted attribute rows pair to real stored disco types, so the numerator loses them too — `appsync/api/apikey`, `bedrock/flow/flowversion`, `cassandra/type`, `datazone/parentdomainunit/domainunit` — and other genuine children (`eks/cluster/insight`, `grafana/workspace/workspaceserviceaccount`, `cases/field/fieldoption`, `access-analyzer/analyzer/finding`) are wrongly demoted. Add the case-insensitive whole-word alternative `(?i)^(id|ids|arn|arns|name|names|identifier|identifiers)$` **alongside** the existing suffix rule, in `refs.go`'s `ownID`/`walkRefs` as well, rather than making the whole regex case-insensitive.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:404` — The service join has no fallback (major, #3)

The only join key is the Smithy sigv4 name, so 14 models whose Service Reference document is filed under another name never see the catalog at all and fall back to shape-only classification: `cloudwatch`→`monitoring`, `resource-groups-tagging-api`→`tagging`, `mturk`→`mturk-requester`, the IoT data planes, `cloudcontrol`, the SSO portal, `partnercentral-*`. The consequence lands squarely on real resources — `monitoring/dashboard`, `metricstream`, `insightrule`, `alarmmuterule` and `anomalydetector` are classified `catalog` and excluded although `cloudwatch.json` lists them as ARN resources and disco stores all five, with `monitoring/alarm` reaching `resource` only by accident. Operation-name containment is a clean join key: CloudWatch's 50 ops are a subset of `cloudwatch.json`, tagging's 9 of `tag.json`, mturk's 39 of `mechanicalturk.json`, cloudcontrol's 8 of `cloudformation.json`. When `srAll[svc]` is nil, pick the SR document whose operation-name set contains every op name of the model, smallest document on a tie.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:650` — The catalog fallback is unconditional (major, #4)

`classify` returns `ClassCatalog` whenever a depth-0 lister's noun matches neither an SR resource name nor an `IsWrite` noun, and for services with no SR document neither lookup runs at all, so such a lister can never be a resource without positive evidence. 48 excluded rows carry a disco type as a result, including `monitoring/dashboard`, `s3/directorybucket` (`aws:s3express:directory-bucket`), `es/domainname` (the real OpenSearch lister), `rds/reserveddbinstance`, `securityhub/enabledstandard` and `fsx/s3accesspointattachment`; of 606 catalog rows, 200 list an element carrying an ARN member or a creation timestamp. Add an element-ARN/element-timestamp rule before the fallback and apply it at depth 0 for `sr == nil` services too, strip descriptor suffixes (`Names`, `Summaries`, `Metadata`, `Arns`, `Details`) from the noun before the `resCanon` lookup, and add a fixture service with no SR document.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:624` — `cross-cutting` counts the subject and its ancestors (major, #7)

Any lister or detail read authorised against three or more catalog resources is classed `attribute`, but a depth-2 resource legitimately carries its grandparent, its parent and itself, so real child resources are demoted. Seven stored types sit in `attribute` with this signal — `identitystore/group/groupmembership`, `deadline/fleet/queuefleetassociation`, `glue/table/partition`, `glue/table/tableoptimizer`, `glue/userdefinedfunction`, `networkmanager/device/linkassociation`, `wafv2/webacl/resource` — and 55 non-tag rows carry it in total. An overlay audit found 12 operations where the rule fired although `sr.resCanon` names the noun (`mediapackagev2:GetOriginEndpoint` with targets `[Channel, ChannelGroup, OriginEndpoint]`; `identitystore:ListGroupMemberships` with `[AllGroupMemberships, Group, Identitystore]`). Count targets minus the subject and its ARN ancestors, and evaluate the `sr.resCanon` match before the cross-cutting rule.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:349` — `route53/tag` is a covered resource (minor, #22)

The row is real and as described — key `route53/tag`, bucket `covered`, sole op `ListTagsForResources`, attributed to the nonsense type `aws:route53:cidr-collection` with ten types folded in — but the stated mechanism is wrong. `splitVerb` strips the qualifier from both spellings, so there is no rule keyed on the operation name; the singular escapes candidacy only because its output is a bare structure, and the plural is admitted because the rule that should have caught it, `classify`'s cross-cutting test, needs three catalog targets and Route 53's action is authorised against exactly two. Two non-resource rows are in the denominator and one in the numerator (`elasticloadbalancing/tag` is the other); every other tag-noun row across AWS lands in `attribute` or `excluded`. In the spirit of the repo's rule-not-list policy, make the generic noun `tag` a non-subject the way `selfStems` already treats `resource`/`target`, which catches `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeTags` too, and add a two-target plural tag op to the fixture.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:283` — Association resources classify as catalog (minor, #17)

`indexSR` records only `Ident(noun)` of the write action, so `AssociateResolverRule` yields `writeNoun["resolverrule"]` and never `resolverruleassociation`; `classify` then falls through to the catalog fallback for every association lister. 18 excluded AWS rows whose key ends in `association` or `attachment` sit outside the denominator, and seven of them are types disco actually stores, so those scanners' work is invisible: `appstream/applicationfleetassociation`, `appstream/userstackassociation`, `codeguru-reviewer/repositoryassociation`, `ec2/securitygroupvpcassociation`, `fsx/s3accesspointattachment`, and two `route53resolver` association types. The counts in the finding are understated (it conflates this with the whole 49-row excluded-with-type set). Also stamp `Ident(noun+"association")`/`Ident(noun+"attachment")` for `Associate`/`Attach`/`Register` verbs — worth noting in the commit that this raises the numerator by ~7 and the denominator by ~18, so the headline percent moves slightly *down* while accuracy goes up.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:90` — Wrapped list payloads are not recognised (minor, #21)

`analyzeOp` counts only list members directly on the output shape, while `refsOf` does descend one level through a single structure member — the asymmetry the finding names. Pinpoint's `GetApps` wraps its collection in `ApplicationsResponse.Item[]` and the Service Reference marks it `IsList=false` (unlike its `GetCampaigns`/`GetSegments` siblings), so neither signal fires: the live row is `mobiletargeting/app | attribute | aws:pinpoint:app`, and its refs prove `refsOf` found the collection `analyzeOp` missed. Enumerating all 431 models, 399 read-verb ops have this wrapped shape and 59 of those have a plural noun, but almost all are rescued by the catalog's `IsList` flag; the genuinely misbucketed set is essentially Pinpoint's dozen rows and exactly one lost covered type. A blind descent would flip all 399 to `shapeList=true` since `Describe`/`Get` are in `listVerbs`, so gate it on the op noun being plural or the inner element's `Ident` matching the op noun.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:629` — SR match is by noun only, so foreign-namespace resources are admitted (minor, #26)

`classify` returns `ClassResource` on a bare `resCanon[nounCanon]` hit with no check that the SR resource's ARN belongs to this service. `ec2.json` genuinely carries a resource named `group` whose ARN is `arn:…:resource-groups:…:group/${GroupName}`, so `ec2/group` is admitted from `GetGroupsForCapacityReservation`; `route53-recovery-cluster/routingcontrol` is admitted through an ARN in the `route53-recovery-control` namespace while the same object is already covered elsewhere. The facet case checks out too: `profile/calculatedattribute` is admitted as a duplicate of the covered definition resource. Only 8 AWS rows are admitted by a foreign-namespace ARN and four are already covered, so the net removable set is three uncovered rows plus the facet — well under 0.5 points. Two corrections: `hasIDs` plays no part (the `resCanon` branch returns before the id test is reached), and a sigv4/arnNamespace/endpointPrefix allowlist would reject `es/application`, `es/datasource` and `servicecatalog/portfolio` outright, since those models' namespaces disagree with their own SR ARNs — verify the `writable-noun` fallback re-admits them before shipping the rule.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:446` (reported as :460) — The SR lookup never tries parent+noun (minor, #24)

`ListVersionsByFunction` yields the noun `Versions` → `lambda/version`, which misses `resCanon` (Lambda's SR names the resource "function version") and keys via `child-uncatalogued`; `ListFunctionVersionsByCapacityProvider` yields `FunctionVersions`, which hits, keying a second entry `lambda/functionversion`. Both rows are live: the first is covered with `aws:lambda:version`, the second is uncovered with signal `sr:resource=function version` — a duplicate of an object disco already stores, wrongly counted as a gap. `resource-explorer-2/` is the same lookup miss with an empty noun. Two spurious uncovered rows of 1,614; under 0.1 point. The cited line is wrong: any parent+noun retry must run before the key is fixed at :446 and before `classify`, not at the `srName` display assignment at :460. The empty-noun key deserves its own assertion — no candidate key should end in `/`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:449` — Shared signing names fold sibling models together (minor, #14)

`serviceKey` returns the sigv4 name first and entries are keyed `svc + "/" + nounCanon`, so ops from sibling Smithy models fold: 40 signing names are shared by more than one model file and 109 rows carry a repeated op label (`rds/dbcluster` carries `DescribeDBClusters` three times, from docdb, neptune and rds). The harm is much smaller than reported. Measuring which rows fold in an op that exists *only* in a sibling module disco imports no SDK package for, exactly three covered rows are inflated — `lex/bot`, `lex/botalias`, `lex/botversion`, which fold Lex Classic's `GetBots`/`GetBotAliases`/`GetBotVersions` into candidates covered solely by the `lexmodelsv2` scanner. The RDS fold is harmless because the row pairs all three types, and wisdom/qconnect and cloudwatch-events/eventbridge are the same service renamed. The "hidden type" claim is false: `connect-campaigns/campaign` lists both types in `discoTypes` and `discoOnly` is 0 — only the singular display field shows one. The proposed endpointPrefix fix only partly works (it splits lex and cloudhsm but leaves docdb/neptune/rds, elasticsearch/opensearch and apigateway v1/v2 folded); the per-module anchoring signal is the part worth keeping.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:367` — Legacy and current models yield two candidates for one resource (minor, #15)

`elasticsearch-service.json` and `opensearch.json` both sign as `es` but their listers use different nouns, so `es/elasticsearchdomain` is a permanently-uncovered candidate for the same physical domains as the covered `es/domain`. The qualifier strip produces the same effect for Lambda: `ListFunctionVersionsByCapacityProvider` keeps `FunctionVersions` while `ListVersionsByFunction` reduces to `Versions`. Nine legacy-noun duplicate rows exist in total but only two distort the ratio, since the rest are uncovered or excluded on both sides. The proposed fold — strip the service word from a noun and merge — is worth prototyping but must be validated against covered rows first: folding the reserved-instance-offering pair is safe, but stripping `Function` from Lambda nouns would collide `lambda/functionurlconfig` with unrelated candidates.

### 3.2 Identity folding and key spelling — structural, small blast radius

#### `internal/sdkinv/norm.go:33` — `Ident` and `Singular` mishandle Latin and irregular plurals (minor, #16)

`Ident` folds only `-ies`/`-yses` then trims trailing `e`/`s`, so `Ident("indices") = "indic"` while `Ident("index") = "index"`, and `Ident("thesauri")` never meets `Ident("thesaurus")` — identities that should meet do not. The visible consequences are nine mis-singularised display keys shipped in `docs/coverage.md` (`clouddirectory/attachedindice`, `gameliftstreams/applicationshadercach`, `iotsitewise/timesery`, `kendra/thesauri`, `license-manager/receivedlicens`, `wafv2/revenuestatisticstimesery` and three more, all AWS) and exactly one double-count: `qbusiness/index` and `qbusiness/indice` are both covered and both map to `aws:qbusiness:index`. The sharper consequence is the scaffold: `gen.go:108` hands a `Singular()` stem straight into a committed Go constant, which is precisely what `norm.go:26-29` tells callers not to do — reproduced, `disco-scaffold gcp:monitoring` emits `TypeMonitoringTimesery = "gcp:monitoring:timesery"` plus a matching `registerType`. Add `-ices`→`-ex/-ix` and `-i`→`-us` to `Ident`, treat `series`/`species` as invariant, fix the `-ches`/`-nses` cases in `Singular`, add `norm_test` pairs, and consider giving `display()` and `gen.go` a shared display-singular helper distinct from the equality-only `Singular`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:539` — Depth is the parent ARN's variable count (major, #8)

`lineage` sets depth to `len(vars)-1`, but ARNs such as `stack/${StackName}/${Id}` carry two variables for one level, and chime, datasync, sso and organizations spell the account slot `${AccountId}`, which the partition/region/account filter does not strip. 251 candidates (95 of them resources) have a depth that is not their parent's depth plus one — `cloudformation/changeset` sits at depth 2 with a depth-0 parent, `chime/appinstance` is parented to a non-existent `<svc>/account` — and 465 candidates name a parent that is not a candidate key. Per-depth percentages and every scaffold hint inherit this. Treat any ARN variable whose lower-cased name is partition, region or account (or ends in those) as scope, and derive depth in a second pass: parent entry depth plus one when resolvable, otherwise the count of ancestor resource segments in the ARN path.

### 3.3 Azure classification — structural, largest single percentage move

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:261` — The class rule ignores the ARM envelope (major, #29)

`classify()` derives the class only from item-path verbs (PUT/PATCH/DELETE → resource, GET/HEAD → catalog) and `inventory.go:169` turns catalog into `BucketExcluded` unconditionally, even when a scanner already stores the type. Re-deriving every catalog row's element model from the cached sources: of 572 catalog rows, 429 elements carry `SystemData` and 88 carry `ID`+`Type` — 517 with the full ARM proxy-resource envelope, against only 16 id-only, 16 with no envelope, 12 with no element and 11 unresolved. 434 of the 572 are depth>0 children, exactly the case the AWS extractor calls a resource, so the two providers' denominators rest on different rules. Moving the 517 into the denominator takes Azure from 19.70% (386/1959) to roughly 16.1% (399/2476): **the published Azure headline is overstated by about 3.6 points and 504 real gaps never appear in the report at all.** The clincher is that 13 catalog-excluded rows already carry a `discoType` — disco scans and stores them as resources while the matrix counts them excluded, which is self-contradictory on its own terms; fix those first. The envelope alone is not sufficient as the full rule (`microsoft.authorization/provideroperations` and `microsoft.advisor/metadata` are genuine non-resources), so pair it with a second discriminator such as depth>0 or a non-tenant scope.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pathtmpl.go:57` — ARM singleton item ids are treated as collection statics (major, #28)

`StripScopes` sets `rp.Item` only when the template's last segment is a `{param}`, so `.../blobServices/default` reads as a two-level collection path; `index()` then falls through to the non-GET rejection, so the PUT on that exact path is discarded into `Universe.Other`, `itemMethods` is empty, and `classify()` stamps `no-item-path` → `ClassNonResource`. 114 rows whose key ends in `/default` are excluded as non-resource, every one of them — including `microsoft.storage/storageaccounts/blobservices/default`, `microsoft.eventhub/namespaces/networkrulesets/default` and `microsoft.network/dnszones/dnssecconfigs/default` — while the cache plainly shows GET+PUT on those paths. Counting distinct ARM templates whose trailing static is `default`/`current`, 136 exist and 89 carry a write verb. Child mis-keying is live too: 55 rows carry a bogus `default` segment inside the key, 19 of them in the uncovered bucket with keys no scanner can ever `Ident`-match. Two evidence items are wrong: `storageaccounts/blobservices/default/containers` is not disco-scanned (the correct statement is that the key is unmatchable if a scanner is ever added), and the "165 candidates have a parent that is not a key" figure is a different defect — only three of those 165 involve `default`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:171` — Alternate listers become separate excluded rows (minor, #39)

`index()` keys entries by namespace plus static path and `classify()` judges each key only by the item methods on that same path, so a GET that lists an existing resource under a different parent gets its own key with no item path and falls to `ClassNonResource`. Replaying the extraction and matching each no-item-path entry's element model against same-module entries that do have write verbs gives 85 such rows: `microsoft.sql/servers/replicationlinks` is excluded/non-resource while `microsoft.sql/servers/databases/replicationlinks` — same `ReplicationLink` element — is covered; `microsoft.web/serverfarms/sites` and `hostingenvironments/sites` sit beside `microsoft.web/sites`. All 85 are excluded so no coverage number moves; the harm is that 85 of 1,785 "non-resource" rows are not non-resources.
