The reporter's scenario of a scanner pairing with such a row does not occur today — the only alternate client disco instantiates uses the primary, covered path. Fold the alternate builders in as extra ops under an `alternate-lister` signal rather than dropping the entry, so a scanner that does use the alternate op still pairs.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:185` — Any non-item GET becomes a candidate (minor, #36)

`index()` keeps any GET whose stripped path does not end in a `{param}` without ever consulting `b.paged` or `b.result`, while `README.md:139` documents the Azure lister rule as a GET builder whose response has `Value []*T`. Reimplementing the extractor over the pinned cache reproduces both the 3,744 candidate total and the reporter's 307 candidates that have no item path and whose every collection GET is neither paged nor decodes into a `Value []*T` — singleton and action GETs such as `microsoft.apimanagement/service/networkstatus`, `.../portalsettings/signin`, `microsoft.alertsmanagement/alertsmetadata` and `microsoft.insights/components/quotastatus`. Cross-checking all 307 against the matrix, every one is `excluded/non-resource`, so the covered/uncovered split and the 19.70% figure are untouched — the effect is confined to the excluded bucket and the op listings. Either enforce `paged || Value[]*` in `index()` and route the rest to `Other`, or amend the README to say what the code does.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/extract.go:261` — Delete-only item paths (minor, #30)

Any item-path DELETE counts as mutability, and GCP does the same thing explicitly under a documented `delete-only` signal. Two of the finding's claims are wrong: strictly delete-only Azure rows number 2, not 35 (the 35 is DELETE-without-PUT/PATCH), and Azure does emit a derivable signal — `classify()` appends one `item:<METHOD>` entry per item verb. The reproducible inconsistency is narrower and sharper: semantically identical soft-delete tombstone listings split three ways purely by which verb the SDK exposes. `microsoft.apimanagement/deletedservices` and `microsoft.cognitiveservices/deletedaccounts` (GET+DELETE) are uncovered resources; `microsoft.keyvault/deletedvaults`, `microsoft.sql/deletedservers`, `microsoft.storage/deletedaccounts` and `microsoft.web/deletedsites` (GET only, purge is a POST) are excluded catalog; three more with no item path are excluded non-resource. That split is a symptom of the GET-only rule in #29, so fix it there rather than by adding a hand-classified `record` class, which the repo's no-hand-lists rule disfavours.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pins.go:12` — Azure's pin is monorepo HEAD, and the skew rows are backwards (minor, #40)

Half of this verifies and half does not. The verified half: all four `sdk-skew` rows are backwards. `armcompute/v6@v6.4.0` and `armappplatform@v1.2.0` — the versions `go.mod` actually imports — ship the CloudServices and AppPlatform `Services` clients, while the cache snapshot (`armcompute` at v8.3.0, no appplatform directory at all) does not: the clients exist in the linked SDK and were *deleted upstream*, so `README.md:190` ("A call the pinned SDK does not ship … bump the pin") and `README.md:325` ("Bumping the pin is the fix") give advice that cannot work — bumping moves the snapshot further from the imported version. The rejected half: scoring all 1,573 uncovered rows against the `go.mod` module versions gives 288 rows whose every op is absent from the imported version and 481 naming a module `go.mod` does not import at all, and **neither group is a defect** — the denominator is deliberately the upstream API surface. Do not pin Azure per `go.mod`; that would delete 769 rows and inflate the reported percentage. The fix is documentary and label-level: say that `AzureSDKRef` is monorepo HEAD, that skew can mean either direction, and that for the removed-upstream direction the fix is a `go.mod` major bump plus retiring the scanner. A pairing test asserting each imported arm module exists in the cache is a useful addition — as a warning surface, not a denominator filter.

#### `internal/providers/azure/azure_coverage.go:60` — 34 Azure resource keys can never match the ARM registry (major, #123)

`RegistryKey` returns `c.Key` verbatim and `CanonicalKey` only lowercases, so any candidate key that is not an ARM type can never match `Providers/List`. Two shapes are affected: 19 covered/uncovered keys carry a mid-path `/default/` segment that the ARM type omits (`microsoft.storage/storageaccounts/blobservices/default/containers` against `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers`, seven `microsoft.avs` workload-network rows, three `microsoft.security` DevOps rows), and 15 resource-class candidates are reachable only through `/locations/{location}` paths that the extractor treats as a scope pair while ARM keeps the prefix in the type name. Each yields a false candidate-only row and, where the ARM twin exists, a paired false registry-only row; 143 further excluded-class keys carry `/default` and degrade the `known[]` side. The reporter's other buckets do not produce candidate-only rows — the `{param}` and `?query` keys are all excluded-class, so the class filter already keeps them out. Strip fixed singleton segments from the comparison key as well as restoring `locations`. (Medium confidence: no Azure credential was reachable, so the ARM side is inferred from the code and the key shapes, not observed.)

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/refs.go:103` — The string-ref rule misses `*URI`/`*URL` and `ManagedBy` (major, #32)

`walkRefs` accepts only `*string`/`[]*string` fields ending in `ID`/`IDs`/`ResourceID`. Re-running the same walk over every non-excluded Azure candidate, 300 rows carry a `*string` field ending `URI`/`URL` within depth 3 — `KeyVaultURI` ×45, `KeyVaultURL` ×20, `KeyVaultKeyURI` ×18, `KeyEncryptionKeyURL` ×17 — and 23 carry a bare `ManagedBy`. The published matrices confirm the asymmetry: zero Azure ref paths end in uri/url against 783 in the GCP matrix, because GCP's `refNameRe` already matches `Link`/`Url`/`Uri` and AWS's matches `Arn`/`Name`. These are edges disco genuinely resolves: `messaging_resolvers.go:89` defines `vaultNameFromVaultURI` and three resolvers build Key Vault edges by parsing exactly these strings, yet the documented `--with-refs` workflow ranks Key-Vault-referencing types as refless leaves. Do not take a blanket URI/URL suffix, which would pull in 100-odd data-plane endpoints and sign-on URLs naming no ARM resource; narrow it to the KeyVault/Key family plus the exact name `ManagedBy`, or gate the bare suffix on a `*KeyVault*`/`*Encryption*` parent path.

#### `internal/sdkinv/azure/refs.go:72` — `refsOf` only understands `Value []*T` (minor, #31)

The test is `f.name == "Value" && strings.HasPrefix(f.typ, "[]*")`, so both the polymorphic `Value []<X>Classification` shape (47 occurrences in the cache) and the `&result.<X>Array)` decode (83 occurrences) miss. For the array case the result type is not in `models.go` at all — it is a field of the response struct in `response_types.go` — so the models table is empty and `refsOf` returns nil. Re-running the ref walk with `response_types.go` added, 18 candidate rows are attributable to the array shape and 2 to the `Classification` shape, but only four actually gain refs once fixed (`microsoft.deploymentmanager/rollouts` gains three, including `Properties.ArtifactSourceID`; two siblings and one PowerBI row gain one to three each). The `Classification` half is near-worthless — two candidates, neither gains a ref. Refs are hints, so no bucket or percentage changes. The array half is cheap: the files are already cached, and parsing them into the same models table is enough.

### 3.4 GCP classification and lister definition — structural, small numbers

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:375` (reported as :444) — Mutable get-only nodes are classed catalog (major, #44)

`classify` tests `insert`/`create`, then `delete`, then `get`, so a node with `get` plus `patch`/`update`/`destroy`/`undelete`/`setIamPolicy` falls into `catalog` and out of the denominator. Re-reading every Discovery node behind each catalog candidate, 31 live candidates are in that state — `secretmanager/secrets/versions` (`access`, `destroy`, `disable`, `enable`), the Bare Metal Solution instances/networks/volumes (with `patch`, `rename`, `reset`, `resize`), `vmwareengine` subnets, `privateca` CRLs, `networkconnectivity/hubs/groups`, `firestore` fields, `containeranalysis/scanconfigs`. This is a genuine defect rather than a style preference because `README.md:96-99` defines catalog as "Provider-published, read-only" and a node with `destroy`/`patch` is not read-only, while the Azure extractor counts an item PATCH as a resource. Five of the 31 are types disco actually scans and stores, so the report calls a covered type excluded. Prefer `has(patch|update|destroy|undelete) → ClassResource` with a `mutable` signal — `setIamPolicy` alone is weak evidence and would pull in four plausible genuine catalogs — which narrows the set to 25, and update the live anchor in `extract_test.go:135`, which currently pins `cloudresourcemanager/organizations` to `ClassCatalog`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:166` (reported as :235) — Only `list`/`aggregatedList` count as listers (minor, #45)

`indexDoc` files a lister only for those two method names and `gcpListerSet` agrees, so a collection enumerated by `search`, `fetch` or `listPolicies` never becomes a candidate. The `cloudresourcemanager/organizations` example reproduces: v1 and v3 expose `search` with no `list`, only v1beta1 has `list`, so the candidate is stamped `preview-only` and shows as `excluded` while carrying a type disco scans. Measuring the rest rather than taking it: across the 192 included APIs exactly 34 nodes are enumerated only by search/fetch/query/listPolicies with no `list` at any version, of which perhaps six are plausible resources (`iam/policies`, two `kmsinventory` protected-resource nodes, `datacatalog/catalog`, `dataform` team folders, `aiplatform` migratable resources) and the rest are genuine search endpoints. The pairing half is true but harmless — `cloudresourcemanager/projects` and `dataflow/jobs` are covered by name match, a weaker anchor but not a wrong one. Narrow the fix to search/fetch/listPolicies on nodes with no `list` in any version and add `Search` to `gcpListerSet`; the proposed shape-based lister definition is over-broad and would mint 313 duplicate or bogus rows from filtered sub-views (`listUsable`, `listManagedInstances`, `listNetworkEndpoints`).

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:229` — `aggregatedList` is never attached to the regional siblings it enumerates (minor, #47)

`indexDoc` files a lister only under the node that declares it, so `compute:healthChecks.aggregatedList` is an op of `compute/healthchecks` alone, even though the response is a map of scoped lists covering the regional twin, and disco lists the regional types exclusively through the base call (`compute_lb_ext_scanners.go:68` says so in a comment: "The separate RegionHealthChecksService.List is redundant with this and intentionally unused"). Nine Compute rows are therefore covered only by the name-match fallback. No bucket, percent or summary number is wrong today, which is why this is minor rather than major — what is inaccurate is the `reason` column claiming weak evidence where a real scanner op enumerates the rows, and the fragility of those nine rows against any tightening of name matching. Register the `aggregatedList` operation on every sibling collection whose element schema matches, under an `aggregated-by:<collection>` signal, or more cheaply let pairing attribute a scanner's `aggregatedList` to both the base key and the scope-prefixed twin.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:361` — `scopeOf` reads the raw template root (minor, #52)

`scopeOf` resolves against `rootOf` of the *raw* template, so anything not rooted in a cloud root falls through to `ScopeGlobal` even when the caller already normalised it: Cloud Run v1's knative path yields root `namespaces` → global although `dropKnativeRoot` stripped the pair, and `storage` buckets carry their project in a required *query* parameter. 145 of 1,850 rows report `global`, and 48 of those also carry a `scope:project` signal — the row contradicts itself, including all 12 Run rows and 10 Storage rows. The effect is confined to presentation and scaffolding (`Row.Scope` reaches the markdown, the table, the CSV and the scaffold's descriptor comment, never bucketing), but `README.md:310` documents Scope as telling the reader whether a listing is per project, so `global` misleads whoever scaffolds a scanner. Two cheap independent fixes: return `ScopeProject` when `dropKnativeRoot` removed a leading namespaces pair or the lister declares a required project/parent query parameter, and pick the most specific scope among a candidate's ops in `inventory.go:138` rather than the first by label — the latter alone corrects all 48 self-contradicting rows.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:139` — `Row.Scope` is the alphabetically first op's scope (minor, #77)

`row.Scope` takes `c.Ops[0].Scope`, and `SortOps` orders by label, so for GCP — where labels are `<api>:<docPath>.list` — `billingAccounts.`, `folders.`, `organizations.` and bare-global nodes all sort ahead of `projects.`. 160 GCP candidates have ops at two or more scopes and 117 rows print a non-project scope although a project-scoped lister exists: 31 are uncovered rows visible in `docs/coverage.md` (line 3978 shows `aiplatform/batchpredictionjobs` as `global` when its signals are `[create, scope:global, scope:project]`), 14 covered, 72 excluded. AWS and Azure are unaffected. The candidate already records every scope as a `scope:<s>` signal, so the fix is purely a ranking choice: project > resource-group/subscription > org > folder > billing-account > tenant > global, or join the distinct set.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:438` — `create` alone makes a resource (minor, #48)

A node with `create` but no `get`/`delete`/`patch` is classed `ClassResource`, so Monitoring's `projects.timeSeries` — methods `[create, createService, list, query]`, a metric-ingestion endpoint — lands in the denominator as an uncovered resource, taking the Monitoring service from 8/9 to 8/10. Indexing every list-bearing node in the cache, only three of 949 `create`-signalled candidates lack `get`/`delete`/`patch`/`update` anywhere, and the reporter's two extra examples are not among them (`cloudprofiler/profiles` has `patch`, `dialogflow` generators has `get`). The proposed rule is therefore harmful: of the three it would reclassify, two (`cloudbilling/subaccounts`, `androiddeviceprovisioning/partners/customers`) are genuine resources that would be wrongly dropped. Either write a narrower rule keyed on the query/aggregation shape, or leave this single row as documented behaviour.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:190` — Two Discovery documents for one API (minor, #56)

`sql/v1beta4` and `sqladmin/{v1,v1beta4}` all carry `rootUrl https://sqladmin.googleapis.com/` with an empty `servicePath` and canonical name "SQL Admin", and `indexDoc` keys candidates by document name, so the same eight collections land twice. All eight duplicates sit in `excluded/preview-only` (the `sql` document ships only v1beta4), so the 23.29% figure, the per-service table and the report are unaffected — the reporter's "five spurious candidate-only rows" is a property of their own cross-check artifact, not of any disco output. Today this is eight redundant excluded rows plus a latent hazard if Google ever publishes a GA `sql` document. The fix must key on `rootUrl` **plus** `servicePath` or `canonicalName`: 31 documents share `https://www.googleapis.com/`, so a rootUrl-only collapse would be catastrophic.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/extract.go:224-227` (reported as :294) — `Required` lists a container placeholder (minor, #54)

The loop exempts a param only when its predecessor is a static scope name, so in the generic `{parent}` expansion `{v2Id}/{v2Id1}/sinks` the first param is skipped by the `i>0` guard and the second is emitted as required. Running the real extractor gives exactly 22 such entries of 1,831 (`v2Id1` ×11, `nodesId1` ×6, `v2betaId1` ×3, `v3Id1` ×2). Nothing user-visible is wrong: `Operation.Required` is written by the extractors and read by *nothing* in production — not the scaffold (which never references the field, contrary to the finding's scenario), not `internal/coverage`, not any subcommand. This is a latent data-quality bug in a write-only field. The proposed guard (`&& !segs[i-1].Param`) is correct and rightly drops the entry rather than replacing it, since the two placeholders together name a container.

#### `internal/sdkinv/gcp/refs.go:32` — Ref heuristics admit JSON-schema keys and display names (minor, #51)

Of 4,990 live GCP refs, 42 end in `jsonSchema.$ref`/`$schema`/`$id`, plus `displayName` ×20, `generateName` ×10, `clientOperationId` ×24, `revisionId` ×20, `cpeUri` ×34 and `redirectUri` ×14. The mechanism is misattributed: the `$`-prefixed names are admitted by `refDescRe` matching their descriptions ("A reference to another schema", "The URI defining…"), not by the `Ref$`/`Id$` name suffixes. The live impact is one orphan row — `gcp:pubsub:schema`, whose only ref is its own `revisionId` — flipping into the derived-leaf set. Worth taking as noise reduction (skip names starting with `$`; add `displayName`, `generateName`, `clientOperationId`, `revisionId` to `ownProps`), but it is not a correctness repair.

### 3.5 Refs extraction on AWS — the resolver worklist's quality

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/refs.go:25` — `refsOf` finds no element for flat or wrapped-with-extras detail reads (**critical**, #2)

`refsOf` recognises only a list-of-structure member or an output with exactly one structure member. A detail read whose output is flat (`GetEnvironment` returning `vpcId`, `subnetIds`, `loadBalancerArn` directly) or which wraps the resource beside `Status`/`RequestId` (`DescribeDashboard` → `[Dashboard, RequestId, Status]`) contributes zero refs, and `--with-refs` then hides the type as a derived leaf needing no resolver. 1,275 of 4,607 `Get`/`Describe`/`Head` ops on candidate rows have such an output, and walking it as the element gives 87 of the 361 hidden AWS orphans real references — `aws:m2:environment` (vpcId, subnetIds, loadBalancerArn), `aws:quicksight:dashboard` (DataSetArns, ThemeArn), `aws:imagebuilder:image`, `aws:iot:encryption-configuration` (kmsKeyArn). These are 87 resolver gaps currently presented to the maintainer as finished work. When no list-of-structure member exists, walk every structure member of the output as an element; when none exists but id-like primitives do, walk the output shape itself at depth 0 with the own id excluded; and extend `idLikeRe` with the whole-word lowercase alternatives (shared with #12).

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/refs.go:76` — `walkRefs` accepts id-like members regardless of target type (minor, #19)

The default case tests only `idLikeRe` against the member *name*, never the target shape, so enum-typed `*Name`, integer ids, idempotency tokens and free-text DNS or device names are emitted as references: `ec2/instance` refs include `State.Name` (an enum), `PrivateDnsName`, `RootDeviceName` and `BlockDeviceMappings.DeviceName`, and `aws:route53resolver:firewall-domain-list`'s only refs are `CreatorRequestId` and `ManagedOwnerName`. The claimed magnitude does not hold: across all 431 models, id-like structure members target `string` 54,129 times against enum 241, integer 109 and long 147 — non-string targets are under 1%, so "~30% of refs" is really "refs ending in Name", most of which (`RoleName`, `BucketName`, `FunctionName`) are correct. Demonstrably wrong refs are roughly 2–3%: 202 Dns/Device/Display/File/Host/User/State-name paths and 72 token-like paths of 11,614. Take the two safe clauses — skip non-string targets, skip a token/ETag/RevisionId name regex — and drop the third: a "known cross-service noun" list is exactly the hand-maintained list the repo forbids.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/refs.go:85` — `ownID` applies only at depth 0 (minor, #18)

`ownID` returns false for any depth>0, so an own id inside a wrapper leaks as a reference: `ec2/instance` emits `Instances.InstanceId` (the element is `Reservation`), and `aws:chime:media-pipeline` ranks #2 of 460 ref-carrying orphans with 17 refs of which 10 are `<Variant>.MediaPipelineArn/Id` re-stated across union arms. The depth-0 half of the claim holds too but is rare (`apigateway/domainname` emits both `DomainName` and `domainName`). Refs have no effect on coverage, but they drive the documented `--with-refs` ranking. Adopt only the nested half — suppress an id at depth>0 when the enclosing member singularises to the candidate noun, or when the wrapper was entered through the single-structure descent. Do **not** adopt "treat a word-prefix of the noun as own at depth 0": that rule matches 682 refs on 571 rows and the overwhelming majority are genuine cross-resource references (`aoss/vpcendpoint`→`vpcId`, `apigateway/apimapping`→`ApiId`, `bedrock/agentalias`→`agentId`), so it would destroy far more signal than it removes.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:785` — Richest-first ordering and the six-ref cut promote noise (minor, #126)

`refsCell` prints the first six sorted paths, so for `aws:chime:media-insights-pipeline-configuration` the eight alphabetically-first refs are all `Elements.AmazonTranscribe*.{LanguageModelName,VocabularyName…}` and the only actionable `ResourceAccessRoleArn` sorts ninth and is cut; `aws:oam:link`, with its single real `SinkArn`, sorts at position 389 of 460. Six of 460 rows are in the first state. The rank inflation itself is not caused by the sort but by `ownID` (#18) — fix that and the noise largely disappears without touching the ordering. The JSON output carries every ref, so this is presentation only.

### 3.6 Pairing attribution — which types a candidate is credited with

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:272` — Every reachable `Type*` identifier counts as stored (major, #58)

`scanBody` marks `f.types[v]` for any `*ast.Ident` naming a `Type*` constant anywhere in the body, and `collectVarTypes` folds a whole package-level table into any function that mentions the variable — with no store-side signal at all. So a resolver that pages a lister purely to emit edges registers as an `emits` pairing. `monitor_resolvers.go` declares `diagnosableTypes` at :30 and uses it only as a `store.ResourceFilter` at :81, and the file's single write is an `UpsertRelationship`; the live report consequently prints `microsoft.insights/diagnosticsettings … DISCO TYPE azure:microsoft.apimanagement:service` with 29 more in `discoTypes`. Re-running the pipeline with idents inside `ResourceFilter` literals, case clauses and comparisons skipped changes eight rows (six AWS, two Azure). The coverage numbers do **not** move, and this is the important correction: the candidate is covered because of the *anchor*, not the types — `BuildInventory` enters every `emits`/`sidecar`/`derived` key into `types` even with an empty set, and a `listed` key is covered with `Reason=sidecar`, which `README.md:206` documents as intended. What is wrong is the reported `discoType`/`discoTypes` and the verify label index, where a diagnostic-settings warning would spuriously "explain" 27 unrelated Azure types. The proposed fix is also incomplete — with those idents skipped, diagnostic settings still picks up three foreign types from `buildLowerIDIndex` read-index calls. Only a positive store signal closes it.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:301` — `Origin` joins types to services by registration *file* (major, #105)

`typeServiceNames` folds in `coverage.ServiceMapper.TypeServices()`, and `internal/restype/origin.go` keys both types and services by `runtime.Caller` file, so the call returns every service registered from the type's source file. A census finds one AWS file (35 types), three Azure and six GCP files in this state — 68 of 248 declared GCP types (27%), eight Azure and 35 AWS. Reproduced: a synthetic `gcp:spanner` error plus one stored row makes 22 types read `scan-error`, of which 11 are `gcp:bigtableadmin:*` and 4 are `gcp:firestore:*` — 15 types blamed on a Spanner failure they cannot come from. `serviceEntry.emits` exists in both the GCP and Azure registries but is set in zero scanner files. Key the service→type join on the registration entry (populate `emits`, or pass descriptors to `registerService`) and fall back to the file only for unclaimed types.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:164` — Candidates the scanners demonstrably list are silently excluded (major, #73)

The class switch runs after the pairing switch and unconditionally wins, so a candidate a scanner provably lists is still bucketed `excluded` and its reason overwritten with the class string, discarding the strongest available evidence that the class rule is wrong. 93 excluded rows carry a disco type they are labelled as not being (AWS 49, Azure 25, GCP 19): `monitoring/dashboard` is `excluded/catalog` while `cloudwatch_scanners.go:233` pages `ListDashboards` and stores it; `microsoft.network/dnszones/recordsets` is `non-resource` while `azure_types.go:183` declares the type; `secretmanager/secrets/versions` is `catalog` while `gcp_types.go:262` declares it. `render_markdown.go:68` makes it invisible — the Excluded section prints only service, key and reason, so the paired type never reaches the reader. Counting those 49 AWS rows as covered moves the AWS headline 50.34% → 51.08%. The attribute half of the finding does not stand: `ClassAttribute` means "Get + id, no collection", and a scanner calling that detail read to enrich a listed parent is the intended shape, plus the Attributes section does print the type. Keep the pairing evidence on excluded rows under a `scanner-lists` signal, add the type column to the Excluded section, and expose a filter so these surface as classifier bugs.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:413` — `bestType` falls back to the alphabetically first paired type (minor, #74)

When no paired type matches by ident or leaf, `bestType` returns `names[0]`. Reimplementing the whole chain against the live matrices, tier-3 fires on 235 rows but is genuinely arbitrary — more than one paired type — on exactly 40 (AWS 35, Azure 2, GCP 3). The worst cases: `microsoft.insights/diagnosticsettings` with 30 paired types displays `azure:microsoft.apimanagement:service`; `compute/regions` with 17 displays `gcp:bigqueryconnection:connection`; `kms/keypolicy` displays `aws:kms:grant` over `aws:kms:key`; `route53/tag` displays `aws:route53:cidr-collection`. Thirty of the 40 are visible in `docs/coverage.md`'s type columns; the other ten are excluded rows whose markdown section prints no type. The remaining 195 tier-3 rows are single-type pairings where `names[0]` is the only and correct answer, so the fix must be conditional: only when more than one type is paired and neither tier matches, leave `DiscoType` empty or mark it `multi-type` and keep the set in `DiscoTypes`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:308` — `derived` pairs an orphan type with every candidate the dispatcher reaches (minor, #63)

When a dispatcher anchors nothing itself, every orphan type is paired with every key in `f.reach`. AWS has 14 such pairings, all from `scanAppSync` and `scanMQ`: `aws:appsync:graphql-schema` is attached to 12 AppSync candidates and `aws:mq:configuration-association` to both MQ rows. Azure has five, attaching `azure:microsoft.resources:subscriptions` to three `microsoft.resources` keys, and because `paired[t] = true` is consulted before `viaOther`, that pairing displaces the honest `sdk-skew:SubscriptionsClient.List` reason the type would otherwise carry. The mechanism itself is legitimate — `scanASCSchemas` synthesises schema rows with no SDK list op at all. No bucket, percent or baseline value changes, and `discoTypes` is JSON-only. Restrict derived pairings to reach keys whose service or ident relates to the orphan type, and let skew and other-op reasons outrank `derived` in `Unpaired`.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:1028` — A shared helper absorbs every caller's types (minor, #64)

When `cur == f`, `reachableTypes` takes inflow from every caller, so a helper that both lists and stores accumulates all callers' `rtype` arguments — proven with a fixture where a second caller of a store helper added its type to the first caller's pairing. The live Azure case checks out: `microsoft.resources/resourcegroups` lists seven `discoTypes` of which five arrive this way (CDN WAF policies, network connections, local network gateways, gateway connections, SaaS applications). But the mechanism is not the one described: `azRGFanoutScan` does not anchor `ResourceGroups.List` itself — it calls a typeless lister whose anchor is *promoted* into it by `emit`'s `typeless` branch, and that promotion plus the `cur == f` inflow rule is what produces the row. One live row, JSON-only column, `Row.DiscoType` still correct there, and each polluting type keeps its own honest pairing, so nothing is mis-explained. Do not drop the `cur == f` rule wholesale — it is correct for a helper that genuinely lists and stores. Target the promoted-anchor case instead. A related variant: GCP `compute/regions` accumulates 17 types because five scanners each promote the same `gcpRegions` anchor.

#### `internal/sdkinv/pairing/pairing.go:751` — `LabelGrammar` is a silent filter (minor, #67)

`scanBody` records a string literal only when `grammar.MatchString(v)` passes, so a label-shaped literal that is off-grammar is invisible to the walker, and there is no `label-malformed` diagnostic anywhere in the kind list — contradicting `README.md:321-322` ("a wrong label is a diagnostic that fails the pairing tests"). The genuinely unchecked set is two Azure labels (`"armdigitaltwins:List"` and `"armmanagementgroups:List"`, both missing the `Client.` segment that 374 of the 376 Azure labels use) plus one GCP concatenation. No report row and no `ScanWarning` is wrong: every candidate those labels belong to is covered by an anchor anyway, and there are zero `label`-kind pairings live. The ~21 off-grammar AWS strings (`amp:ListWorkspaces(extended)`, `cloudfront:ListDistributions (monitoring)`) are deliberate human-readable decorations for the operator-facing warning, not typos. Add a loose shape detector for the two provider-specific near-miss forms only, stripping the trailing decoration before resolving, and do not diagnose the decorated AWS labels or the `"prefix:"+expr` concatenations.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:137` — `Row.Ops` repeats the same op label (minor, #72)

`row.Ops = append(row.Ops, op.Label)` never dedupes and `SortOps` does not fold equal labels, so GCP per-version documents and AWS sibling models produce repeats: 930 rows across the three matrices render a duplicated ops cell (AWS 109, Azure 3, GCP 818 — 818 of roughly 1,900 rows). `apigateway/authorizer` reads `GetAuthorizer, GetAuthorizer, GetAuthorizers, GetAuthorizers`; `compute/licenses` reads `licenses.list` three times. It reaches three user surfaces — the markdown Uncovered and Attributes tables, the CSV, and the scaffold comment — with GCP's uncovered table, the main work queue, worst hit. Buckets, depth, parent and percentages are untouched since `Ops` is never read back, so this is report noise rather than accuracy loss. Fold same-label operations in the extractors (union their modules, OR `IsList`/`Paged`), or minimally `slices.Compact` the labels after the loop.

### 3.7 `coverage verify`'s reason column — the command's whole output

Beyond the four confirmed bugs (#101–#104), five accuracy findings make the same column wrong in normal operation.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:239` — verify ignores the scan's service and region scope (major, #106)

`scanContext.load` unmarshals only `providers` from the scan's scope, although `cmd/scan.go:477-484` also persists `scope.<provider>.services` and `.regions`, and `reason()` never consults either — so a `--services`-filtered scan is indistinguishable from an empty account. Reproduced: a scan scoped to `aws:ec2` with one stored instance row reports `no rows` for 1,842 of 1,843 AWS types, while the command's own help documents `no rows` as "the account has none". The provider level already has an `out-of-scope` reason, so the service level is a gap rather than a design choice, and this is a documented, ordinary flag combination making 99.9% of the report's reason column wrong — major, not minor. The fix must handle the polymorphic scope value (a JSON array, or the literal string `"all"`) and match CLI service names through the same `stripProvider`/`typeServiceNames` join used for error entries. The same gap exists for regions.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:277` — A provider that stored nothing and recorded no error explains everything as `no rows` (major, #100)

Both halves check out. On the verify side, a live Azure scan (`completed`, 0 rows, no errors, no warnings) verifies as 417 identical `no rows` rows, and the branch at :277 declines to use the distinguishing bit it has (`!c.stored[provider]` with empty errors). On the scanner side, `enumerateSubscriptions` returns `(nil, nil)` when the pager yields no subscriptions — only the pin path and the config-list path fail closed on `len == 0` — so a credential that can reach no subscription at all produces a `completed` scan with zero rows, no error and no warning, and a wrong-tenant credential is indistinguishable from an empty tenant in both the scan record and the report. Split the severity: the verify rows are under-informative (a one-line cmd-side fix — emit one aggregate reason such as "nothing stored: the scan recorded no failure for azure"), while the substantive half is the scanner, which should `ReportWarning` or fail partial when the enumerate path resolves to zero subscriptions. That half is pre-existing code the coverage work merely made visible.

#### `internal/providers/gcp/gcp_hierarchy.go:42` — GCP hierarchy denials are silently skipped (major, #108)

`scanHierarchy` does a bare `if isPermissionDenied(err) { continue }` at three call sites — `Projects.Get`, `Organizations.Get`, `Folders.Get` — with no `skipIfDenied`, no warning and no error, while `internal/providers/gcp/CLAUDE.md:90` states the rule as "always pair with `skipIfDenied`". A denied `Projects.Get` also leaves `projCache` empty, so the project-upsert loop skips the row entirely, and `runOrgServices` returns immediately when no scope resolved, emitting neither an error nor a notice. Since `reason()` consults only errors and warnings, the three hierarchy types plus the org-scope service types — roughly 28 to 39 declared GCP types — read `no rows` on a project-scoped credential with nothing recorded anywhere, and the operator's `disco scan` output never mentions the denial either. The reporter's "246 of 246" overstates the share attributable to this mechanism; the rest read `no rows` for unrelated reasons that `reason()` does not consult at all. Add `skipIfDenied` at the three continues and a recorded notice from `runOrgServices`.

#### `internal/providers/gcp/gcp_scanner.go:228` — One transient error aborts the whole GCP provider (major, #109)

`scanProject` builds an `errgroup.WithContext` and returns any error that is not one of the three sentinels — including the five-minute per-service timeout firing, or a 500. The errgroup then cancels every sibling service in every project, `g.Wait()` propagates out of `Scan`, and the runner records `Provider: gcp, Service: "scan"`, which verify's whole-scan rule blames for every missing type. This directly violates `internal/providers/CLAUDE.md:54` ("Replace `errgroup.WithContext` with a plain `sync.WaitGroup` for per-service fan-out — errgroup cancels siblings on first error, which we explicitly do not want"), which AWS and Azure both follow. Filed as accuracy, it is really a scan-behaviour bug: the run keeps its phase-1 rows and loses **all** relationship edges, because phase 2 never runs. Reject the second half of the proposed fix — since errgroup cancellation genuinely invalidates the rest of the run, verify blaming `gcp:scan` is the correct reading. Fix only the dispatcher: report the per-service error with the service name and the project scope, return nil, and drop the errgroup.

#### `internal/providers/azure/azure_scanner.go:367` — Ad-hoc Azure error labels match no type (minor, #107)

`reportPanic(st, "entra", …)` and `ReportError{Service: "resourcegroups"}` use labels that `typeServiceNames` does not know: the registered tenant service is `azure:microsoft.entra`, and `resourcegroups_scanners.go` registers no service at all. Reproduced with synthetic scans: with those labels, all 416 declared types read `no rows`; with `azure:resources` and `azure:azure:microsoft.entra` the resource-groups type and the four Entra types read `scan-error` correctly. Severity is minor rather than major because a broadly-denied credential stores nothing at all, in which case the `!c.stored[provider]` fallback already explains every type — the mislabel only bites when other services stored rows, and then it costs at most five rows. The `providers` half of the finding is not a defect: the RP-registration probe is explicitly non-fatal, so its warning loses no type and correctly explains none. Fix only the two error labels.

#### `cmd/coverage_verify.go:262` — `scan-error` reasons drop the message (minor, #99)

The reason carries only `e.Code` plus region, while the warning branch twelve lines below includes a truncated message, and `scanrun.scanErrorCode` substring-matches a ten-string allowlist and otherwise returns the literal `"Error"`. On the live AWS scan, all 32 scan-error rows read exactly `scan-error: Error (us-west-2)` while the persisted entry holds a 367-character message: `iot:ListSecurityProfiles: … UnauthorizedException: This feature is no longer available to new customers`. The reason is right in kind and useless in content whenever the SDK code falls outside the allowlist, which is most of the time (the list contains neither `UnauthorizedException` nor `ValidationException`). Mirror the warning branch — render code, optional service and region, then the truncated message — and optionally widen `scanErrorCode` to parse the `api error <Code>:` fragment the AWS SDK always emits.

#### `internal/scanrun/scanrun.go:225` — Error entries lose their scope and always carry code `Error` (minor, #111)

`ScanErrorEntry` carries only service, region, code and message while `ScanWarningEntry` carries `Scope`, so `persistErrors` drops the scope and verify renders a bare `scan-error: Error` with nothing to act on — 100% of Azure and GCP error entries, and even an AWS entry in the live DB reduced to `"Error"`. `scanErrorCode`'s ten-token allowlist also contradicts `ScanErrorEntry`'s own doc comment, which promises a synthesised `transient`/`auth`/`throttle` for non-AWS providers. The Azure region scenario does not hold — Azure scope labels never contain a slash — but the reachable case is the GCP *warning* path, where seven `skipIfDenied` sites pass `project/scope/name` and `regionFromScope` records an instance-group or table name as the region, which verify then prints where a region belongs. Add `Scope` to `ScanErrorEntry`, parse `Region` only for AWS, and either synthesise non-AWS codes or drop the promise from the doc comment.

#### `store/scans.go:450` — `TypesForScan` counts resolver placeholder rows (minor, #110)

`InsertResourcesIfAbsent` hard-codes `reference_only = TRUE` while still writing `discovered_by` and `verified_by` with the scan id, and `TypesForScan` selects on those two columns with no `reference_only` guard, so a stub counts as a type the scan emitted. Seven resolvers insert such stubs, for `gcp:…:project`, `aws:iam:account` and `azure:…:subscriptions`. No live row is wrong — the real database holds one `reference_only` row and a genuine row of the same type exists in the same scan — so this is latent; it bites when the placeholder is the sole row of its type, for example the denied-`Projects.Get` path of #108 combined with a cross-project IAM binding. `TypesForScan` has exactly one caller, so adding `AND NOT reference_only` is safe.

### 3.8 Cross-check drift — the `--cross-check` buckets do not measure drift

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:227` — Both AWS drift buckets are dominated by modelling artifacts (major, #122)

The cross-check treats every resource candidate absent from the registry and every registry resource absent from the universe as drift, but the Service Reference models ARN-bearing authorisation targets, not listable collections, so the two sides are structurally incomparable. Joining the live run's 1,406 candidate-only keys against the universe and the SR: 775 (55%) are depth≥1 child collections whose *parent's* registry key is present — the SR models the parent ARN and never the child collection, so the child can only ever read as drift — 443 are depth-0, of which 45 sit in services with no SR document at all, and 142 have an unresolvable parent. Separately, a same-service near-name join finds 132 candidate-only rows that have a registry-only twin naming plainly the same resource (`autoscaling/policy` ↔ `AWS::AutoScaling::ScalingPolicy`, `amplify/domainassociation` ↔ `AWS::Amplify::Domain`, `bedrock/provisionedmodelthroughput` ↔ `AWS::bedrock::provisioned-model`), so roughly 132 of the 587 registry-only rows are the other half of the same double count. The actionable residue is a small fraction of the 1,993 rows the command prints. Note the reporter's counts came from a replay whose CFN half was scraped from git history; the live figures are 1,406/587, not 1,620/427. Define drift with the SR's own model, and file everything else as "unmodelled by SR" or no row at all.

#### `internal/providers/gcp/gcp_coverage.go:246` — `hasFetchMethod` counts get-only nodes (major, #120)

The registry walk emits a type for any node with `get`, `list` or `aggregatedList`, while the universe only ever creates candidates from listers, so every get-only Discovery node is structurally unkeyable and lands in registry-only by construction. Classifying the live registry-only rows with an independent walker over the 355 cached Discovery APIs: 104 of 156 have no `list`/`aggregatedList` anywhere in that API's documents, 7 have a list (the actionable residue) and 45 could not be checked because the live Discovery list carries APIs the Go-client cache lacks. Sample rows: `apigee/{aliases,data,flowhooks,keys,keystores}`, `aiplatform/{responses,skills,servingProfiles}`. The GCP registry-drift output therefore overstates real drift by roughly 7x. Keep the get-only nodes visible under a distinct `unlistable` reason rather than discarding them — a get-only mutable node is real information, it just is not drift.

#### `internal/providers/aws/aws_coverage.go:157` — Unioning CloudFormation `ListTypes` into the registry (minor, #121)

Re-implementing `CanonicalKey` and diffing against the 2,308 cached Service Reference canon keys, 167 of the 587 live registry-only rows exist only because CFN is unioned in, and 216 rows display a PascalCase CFN service spelling next to lowercase SR spellings across 74 distinct service strings. Rows such as `AWS::EC2::EIP`, `AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy`, `AWS::Route53::RecordSet`, `AWS::Lambda::Url` and 15 `AWS::CloudFormation::*` entries do duplicate resources the universe has under another noun. Severity is minor because most of the 167 are CFN template constructs with no standalone list API (`SecurityGroupIngress`, `SubnetRouteTableAssociation`, `VPCGatewayAttachment`, `UserToGroupAddition`) — literally-true registry entries rather than manufactured falsehoods — and the case-spelling problem is cosmetic. The flagship example is wrong: `AWS::SQS::Queue` is *not* CFN-contributed, its canon is in the Service Reference, and it is genuine drift caused by finding #1. Do **not** drop CFN from the union: CFN's spelling is what matches several disco nouns the SR renames (`elasticache/cachecluster` matches `AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster` while the SR calls it `cluster`), so dropping it converts those into new candidate-only rows. Keep CFN under a distinct `cfn-only` reason with the service segment normalised for display.

#### `internal/coverage/inventory.go:212` — `CrossCheck` collapses candidates sharing a `RegistryKey` (minor, #79)

`candidates` is a `map[string]Candidate` keyed by a leaf-only identity for both GCP and AWS, so colliding candidates overwrite and at most one candidate-only row can be emitted per id. Measured collisions among resource-class rows: GCP 56 colliding ids hiding 75 sibling candidates, AWS 8 hiding 8 (the documented `…Resource` suffix folding). The impact claim does not survive, though: rebuilding the upstream set from the cached Discovery corpus with the registry walker's own rule gives 18 candidate-only rows emitted against 19 possible — exactly one hidden row. Keep the cheap half of the fix (make `candidates` a `map[string][]Candidate` and emit one row per unseen candidate) and drop the other half: the registries publish no paths at all (GCP gives collection leaf names, CFN and the SR give type names), so there is nothing for a path-keyed comparison to compare against.

### 3.9 Documentation and tests that state something untrue

#### `README.md:195` — Public users get a name-matching-only percentage (major, #85)

Outside a checkout, `defaultSourceRoot` returns empty — which is every installed-binary invocation — and the documented command then prints AWS 43.23%, Azure 19.6% and GCP 18.9%, with a key-by-key diff showing 231 AWS, 3 Azure and 44 GCP keys flipping covered → uncovered. `ec2/address` and `monitoring/alarm` are among them, so 278 resources disco actually scans are printed as gaps, contradicting `docs/coverage.md` by 7.1 points on AWS. The marker is better than reported — `-o json` emits a top-level `"pairing": false` and every run prints the stderr warning — so the precise gap is CSV and JSONL, whose rows carry nothing. The accuracy loss is inherent to a shipped binary, since pairing needs disco's own source, so the actionable half of the fix is the README caveat plus a per-row or per-stream pairing marker; build-time embedding of the pairings is a design change, not a bug fix.

#### `cmd/coverage.go:155` — `--services` matches only the SDK spelling (minor, #93)

`Filter` matches solely on `strings.ToLower(r.Service)` — the sigv4 name — and never the disco service segment of `r.DiscoType`; `disco-scaffold`'s `splitService` does the same. `disco coverage services --providers aws --services cloudwatch` prints the header row and nothing else while the summary line still reports the unfiltered 50.3%, whereas `--services monitoring` returns 17 rows including `monitoring/alarm → aws:cloudwatch:alarm`. 67 AWS disco service names and one Azure name match no row at all. This is usability rather than accuracy, and the mitigations matter: the flag help says "matched against the row's service segment", the rendered table's SERVICE column shows the SDK spelling, and the scaffold fails with a legible exit-1 message. The genuinely silent case is the zero-row filter with an unchanged summary line. Match `r.Service` or the disco segment, and warn when a `--services` value matched nothing.

#### `internal/sdkinv/aws/extract.go:474` — Every AWS operation is stamped `Scope=account` (minor, #20)

Both call sites hard-code `sdkinv.ScopeAccount`, and all 5,561 AWS candidate rows carry it, while `README.md:310` tells the reader that Scope says whether a listing is per region, per account, per subscription or per project — a promise the AWS side never keeps, so `iam/role` and `ec2/instance` render identically. The column ships in the markdown Uncovered table, in CSV, in JSON and in every scaffolded descriptor comment. Under `sdkinv.go:17`'s own definition ("the container a list operation enumerates within"), `account` is defensible for AWS, so this is a doc mismatch rather than a wrong result. The proposed fix does not work: both `iam.json` and `ec2.json` declare a `Region` parameter in their endpoint rule set, so deriving globality from that parameter would label IAM regional. Either leave Scope empty for AWS (the renderers already dash an empty value) and reword the README and help text to say Scope is provider-specific, or derive globality from the endpoint partition rules.

#### `internal/coverage/CLAUDE.md:72` — The skip-key count undercounts by 67 (minor, #128)

Re-running the deleted reconcile report from `70a08029^` prints `skip-contradicted 198` and `skip-is-child 67`; the test sends an uncovered skip key with depth>0 to the second bucket and only depth 0 to the first, so the two are the same kind of thing and the real count of skip-labelled keys in the uncovered denominator is 265, not the 198 quoted. A reader takes away "~200 reviewed true gaps". Its practical effect is on the ratchet's baseline story: a future rule fix that correctly removes one of those 67 reads as lost coverage rather than a correction. Rewrite as "198 depth-0 + 67 child = 265", and leave the "honest" wording to whoever adjudicates the identity findings rather than asserting it is false.

#### `internal/sdkinv/README.md:99` — The canonical Azure catalog example does not exist (minor, #129)

`grep -c resourceskus matrix-azure.json` returns 0: the key `microsoft.compute/resourceskus` offered as the worked example for the `catalog` class is not a key the extractor produces. The key it actually produces from `armcompute:ResourceSKUs.List` is `microsoft.compute/skus`, and its live row is `excluded / non-resource / [no-item-path, scope:subscription]` — so both halves of the example are wrong. Azure does have 572 real catalog rows; `microsoft.networkcloud/rackskus` is a verified live replacement. The cost is that the canonical worked example cannot be checked against the tool, in a README whose stated purpose is that a surprising row can be explained without a debugger.

#### `internal/providers/gcp/CLAUDE.md:35` — Instructions still point at the retired `Leaf` flag (minor, #130)

The line ends with "triage via a `Leaf: true` flag on the scanner's `coverage.TypeDecl` (AWS precedent: `internal/providers/CLAUDE.md` "Leaf")", but `grep -rn Leaf` across the relevant packages returns nothing — commit `5f6a4ac9` removed the field from both `restype.Descriptor` and `coverage.TypeDecl` — and `internal/providers/CLAUDE.md:117` now reads "There is no `Leaf` flag", so the pointed-at section says the opposite of what the pointer promises. A contributor who follows it gets an unknown-field compile error. The "~216 of 247 emitted types" figure in the same sentence is stale by 2.4x; the live GCP orphan list is 89. Replace with the `coverage resolvers --missing --with-refs --providers gcp` command and a pointer to the corrected section, and land it together with the `TypeRefs` fix, since that command currently hides 46 of the 89.

#### `cmd/coverage_servicemap_test.go:49` — The "unknown scanner service" assertion can never fire (minor, #131)

Probing the live registries, all 2,066 type→service mappings carry the `<provider>:` prefix, so `!strings.HasPrefix(s, p.Name()+":")` never evaluates true and the second assertion is dead. The escape is load-bearing: six service names are unknown to `ServiceNames()` (`gcp:cloudidentity`, `gcp:iam-org`, `gcp:cloudresourcemanager-tags`, `gcp:vpcsc`, `azure:microsoft.entra`, `azure:microsoft.management`, covering 38 types), because `ServiceNames()` is built from filtered services only while `registerOrgService`/`registerTenantService` also note the service on the type origin. The stated consequence is refuted, though: `coverage verify` joins through `TypeServices()`, not `ServiceNames()`, and the org/tenant scanners report errors under the identical literal, so verify joins them fine; the only production consumer of `ServiceNames()` is a progress-column width where every org/tenant name is shorter than its provider's widest. This is a test-only strengthening — add the tenant/org registries to a test-only `AllServiceNames()` and drop the prefix escape, or delete the loop as structurally unenforceable.

#### `internal/coverage/baseline_test.go:103` — `TestBaselineRoundTrip` does not perform a second write (minor, #134)

The body writes once, reads once, asserts `DeepEqual` and one key ordering, and checks the missing-file error — there is no second write and no `bytes.Equal`, so the doc comment's claim of byte-stability across two writes is unasserted. The sub-claim about the mechanism is only half right: stability comes from `encoding/json` sorting map keys **and** from `NewBaseline`'s three explicit `sort.Strings` calls, which the existing key check does cover. The proposed fix also aims at the wrong path — production never writes from a read result; `gen-coverage` writes from `NewBaseline` and `check-coverage` diffs the markdown. Either trim the comment to what is tested, or assert that two `NewBaseline`→`WriteBaseline` runs over matrices supplied in different order produce identical bytes, which is the property that actually matters.

## 6. Recommended order of work

**Tier 1 — cheap, local, each fixes measured wrong output (no headline movement).** Start here; every item is a contained change with a clear test.

1. **#27** Azure `handleRe` per-function bounding — restores refs for 106 listers, one regex plus a fixture. Biggest single recall win in the repo for the effort.
2. **#75 + #125** `TypeRefs` folding `Row.DiscoTypes`, then stop `--with-refs` hiding zero-ref types silently — un-hides 14 provably-referenced orphans and stops 477 types vanishing from the resolver worklist on a hint's absence.
3. **#97, #104, #101, #98** the `coverage verify` reason column: prefix scan-ids, `scan:interrupted`, the Azure per-subscription label plus `Scope` on `ScanErrorEntry`, and the two-pass error match. Four small changes that between them fix the command's entire output in four common situations.
4. **#116** `canonResource` trim-before-`Ident` — 11 wrong drift rows, one line plus a test case whose stem ends in `e` or `s`.
5. **#46, #42, #35, #38, #53** the small GCP/Azure extractor repairs (wrong element pick, unlowered parent, query strings in templates, the `rel[:-1]` panic, the missing cycle guard).
6. **#92, #95, #96, #94** the CLI consistency set (`--write` ignoring `--source-root`, output-format validation on `sdk`, `--providers` normalisation in one place, the CRLF `go.mod`).
7. **#132** raise the walk-time bound so the CI gate stops flaking.

**Tier 2 — restore the gates. These change no number but are the reason a number can be trusted.** Do them before any structural work, because the structural work is exactly what they must police.

8. **#84 + #83** one guard in `runCoverageServices`: refuse `--check-strict`/`--baseline`/`--write-baseline` when any matrix has `!m.Pairing`, and record and compare a `pairing` bool in `ProviderBaseline`.
9. **#82** make `DriftNoBaseline` fatal, merge partial `--write-baseline`, and compare `Pins` line counts before choosing the Makefile branch.
10. **#86** record the Service Reference index sha256 in `pins.go` so it is a real pin, and key the CI cache on the baseline's pins.
11. **#112** spec fingerprint in the cache manifest plus `internal/sdkinv/*/*.go` in the CI cache key.
12. **#78, #81, #88, #89** the remaining gate gaps: explicit `Paired` flag, walking `pb.UncoveredKeys`, write-then-`mv` for the report, rebase before push.
13. **#57** deterministic callee iteration in `walkCallees`, with a byte-stability test.

**Tier 3 — the accuracy work that moves the headline.** Each of these changes a published percentage, so each needs its own commit, its own baseline re-write and a line in the commit message saying which direction and why.

14. **#29** the Azure ARM-envelope rule — **the largest single correction in the review**: Azure 19.70% → ~16.1%, 504 real gaps surfaced. Fix the 13 self-contradicting rows (a scanner stores it, the matrix calls it excluded) first as a separable, indefensible subset.
15. **#73** stop the class switch discarding pairing evidence — 93 rows, AWS 50.34% → 51.08% if counted, and it converts silent classifier bugs into a visible, filterable list that will drive items 16–19.
16. **#10** narrow `writable-noun` to lifecycle verbs — removes 134 uncloseable rows from the AWS denominator (headline up).
17. **#11** the singular-noun `detail-read` carve-out from `shape-list` — 26 certain, ~90 probable rows (headline up). Keep the override itself; 516 covered rows depend on it.
18. **#12** case-insensitive whole-word ids — recovers 65 rows, four of them stored types (headline up, and the numerator gains).
19. **#3 + #4** the SR op-containment join and the element-ARN rule before the catalog fallback — recovers CloudWatch, S3 Express and ~46 other scanned types from `excluded` (headline up).
20. **#1** the primitive-list collection rule — puts `aws:sqs:queue` into the universe at all. Small numerically, but it is the one finding where a top-tier resource is simply missing.
21. **#44** GCP mutable-node rule (`patch|update|destroy|undelete` → resource) — 25–31 candidates, five of them stored (headline moves both ways).
22. **#119, #45** the GCP bucket repairs that stop the same candidate being both out-of-scope and drift.
23. **#127** last in this tier, because it depends on all of the above: state the denominator's definition in the report header and split the headline and per-service table by admitting rule, after the depth>0 asymmetry is closed.

**Tier 4 — bug-only, no percentage effect, but the dev tooling is currently unsafe.**

24. **#90 + #91** the scaffold: consult the registry before emitting `registerService`, and include parent segments in type strings and const names. As shipped, `--write` produces a non-compiling or init-panicking file for 162 targets.

**Tier 5 — refs precision and presentation, once recall (item 1–2) is fixed.**

25. **#18, #19, #32, #31, #33, #51, #126** — `ownID` at depth, target-type filtering, the Azure KeyVault URI family, the `<X>Array` response shape, `zz_generated_models.go` with tag stripping, the `$`-prefixed GCP schema keys, and the ref ordering. None changes a bucket; together they decide whether `resolvers --missing --with-refs` is worth reading.
26. **#2** the flat and wrapped-with-extras element walk. Rated critical by the reporter and it is the single biggest refs-recall item (87 hidden orphans), but it is a larger change than the rest of this tier and should land with a fixture per output shape.

**Tier 6 — documentation, last, and all in one pass.**

27. **#85, #20, #128, #129, #130, #40, #131, #134** — the README's public-user caveat and the `pairing:false` marker on CSV/JSONL, the AWS Scope claim, the skip-key count, the Azure catalog example, the retired `Leaf` pointer, the `AzureSDKRef` skew wording, and the two test-comment corrections. Per the repo's own rule about a standalone public CLI versus the SaaS scanner, fix every surface of each claim in a single pass rather than one file per round.
